course: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 - 6 Practice Exams Set 1 (Udemy)
note: Paraphrased study set: questions and explanations rewritten in our own words; domains and correct answers as revealed in practice mode.

questions.question: Which of these routing protocols is an exterior protocol that runs between different autonomous systems?
questions.why: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol used to exchange routes between autonomous systems; OSPF, EIGRP and RIP work inside one system.

questions.question: A switch linked to several end devices is logging a rising number of CRC errors. What should you investigate first?

choices.text: The speed settings on the switch ports
The quality and type of the cables between the switch and the devices

questions.correctText: The quality and type of the cables between the switch and the devices
questions.why: CRC errors usually come from the physical layer, so cabling is the first thing to check.

questions.question: Someone is setting up wireless in a crowded apartment complex and wants the frequency band with the least interference. Which band should they pick?
questions.why: The 6 GHz band is the newest and least congested, so it suffers the least interference.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using dynamic inventories in networking?

choices.text: Simpler management with less manual work

questions.correctText: Simpler management with less manual work
questions.why: Dynamic inventories mainly simplify management by cutting down manual effort.

questions.question: Traffic sent to a newly added remote network is being dropped. What should you check first?
questions.why: The routing table decides where packets go; a missing or wrong route to the new network drops the traffic.

questions.question: Which connector is terminated on a Cat 5e cable?
questions.why: Cat 5e Ethernet uses RJ-45 connectors, the standard Ethernet plug.

questions.question: Which document is a non-legally binding agreement that sets out actions the parties intend to take together?
questions.why: A memorandum of understanding (MOU) records intended common actions without being legally binding.

questions.question: When should the troubleshooting methodology be used?

choices.text: Only as a last resort after trying random fixes
Only for outages affecting many users
Whenever a network issue is encountered, whatever its size

questions.correctText: Whenever a network issue is encountered, whatever its size
questions.why: The systematic methodology applies to every network problem, regardless of scope or complexity.

questions.question: Users report sluggish speeds and intermittent connectivity, and the router is severely congested. What is the most likely cause?
questions.why: A heavily congested router drops packets, and that loss shows up as slow, intermittent performance.

questions.question: In a criminal or government investigation, what is the process of identifying, recovering and exchanging stored electronic information called?
questions.why: eDiscovery covers finding, recovering and exchanging electronic information for an investigation.

questions.question: For a company's long-term survival through a disaster, which of these matters most?
questions.why: Data is what a business cannot lose; off-site backups survive even if the site is destroyed.

questions.question: A college cafeteria needs wireless coverage using as few access points as possible. Which antenna gives the best coverage for that goal?
questions.why: An omnidirectional antenna radiates in all directions, and high gain stretches the coverage so fewer APs are needed.

questions.question: Which device actively blocks outside attackers before they reach the internal network?
questions.why: An IPS detects and actively prevents threats; an IDS only detects and alerts.

questions.question: Why would an administrator choose static routing over dynamic routing for a segment?

choices.text: To reduce the need to configure routers
To control the exact path traffic follows

questions.correctText: To control the exact path traffic follows
questions.why: Static routes are chosen when the administrator wants full control over the exact path traffic takes.

questions.question: During a wide-scale outage, a theory about a faulty switch module has been tested. What is the next step in the methodology?

choices.text: Determine whether anything has changed on the switch
Document the findings and actions so far

questions.why: After a theory is established and tested, the next step is to establish a plan of action.

questions.question: Which command shows an interface's operational status and settings in detail?
questions.why: show interfaces gives detailed status and settings for each interface.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of static routing?

choices.text: It adapts automatically to topology changes
It uses complex algorithms to pick the best path

questions.why: Static routing means an administrator manually configures every route.

questions.question: Which command tells you whether interface Ethernet0/0 is running OSPF or EIGRP?
questions.why: show route displays the routing table, including which protocol supplied each route.

questions.question: You are pulling new UTP cable from a spool and need to cut it to length. Which tool do you use?
questions.why: A cable snip (cutter) is made for cutting cable to length from a spool.

questions.question: An existing wireless network is limited by too few non-overlapping channels and heavy channel congestion. Which standard should be implemented?
questions.why: 802.11ac runs on 5 GHz with many more non-overlapping channels; 802.11b/g on 2.4 GHz have only three (1, 6, 11).

questions.question: A brand-new fiber link between a router and a switch has no connectivity. What is a likely quick fix?

choices.text: Replace the switch with a faster model
Change the duplex setting on the switch port
Swap the fiber strands at one end

questions.correctText: Swap the fiber strands at one end
questions.why: Swapping the strands at one end fixes a TX/RX mix-up, a common cause of dead fiber links.

questions.question: Speeds are slow with intermittent drops, and you have formed a theory that DHCP is at fault. What comes next?

choices.text: Restart the DHCP server since it is the likely cause
Test the theory to determine the cause
Document the issue and everything done so far
Escalate to a senior administrator right away

questions.correctText: Test the theory to determine the cause
questions.why: Methodology order: identify the problem, form a theory, then test the theory before changing anything.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used when a client retrieves email from a mail server?
questions.why: Port 110 is POP3, used by clients to pull mail down from a server.

questions.question: A company wants a dependable, high-speed link between headquarters and a branch office with steady bandwidth and low latency. Which option fits best?
questions.why: A dedicated leased line gives one customer consistent bandwidth and low latency between two sites.

questions.question: In RSTP, what is the role of the Alternate Port?

choices.text: A non-designated port that discards frames and acts as a general backup in the topology
A backup for the root port that takes over if the forwarding path fails
A port that forwards immediately if the designated port fails
An extra port reserved for management and configuration

questions.correctText: A backup for the root port that takes over if the forwarding path fails
questions.why: The Alternate Port backs up the Root Port and stays blocking until the root path fails.

questions.question: A UPS battery died. What would have let the battery be replaced without shutting down the server?

choices.text: Give the server a redundant power supply
Replace the UPS with a generator
Put a second UPS in the rack

questions.correctText: Give the server a redundant power supply
questions.why: A redundant PSU keeps the server running from another feed while the UPS is off for its battery swap.

questions.question: Latency is high when users open cloud applications. What is the best action to bring latency down?
questions.why: Optimizing routing paths sends traffic over the most efficient routes, which cuts latency.

questions.question: Which device, combined with a lockable feature, improves physical security?
questions.why: Servers in lockable racks are physically protected against unauthorized access and removal.

questions.question: Which antenna type sends its RF signal in one specific direction along a narrow path?
questions.why: A unidirectional (directional) antenna focuses its signal in a single direction with a narrow beam.

questions.question: Endpoints are exchanging unusual traffic and sensitive data went to an unauthorized device because the address resolution table was tampered with. What attack is this?
questions.why: ARP spoofing poisons the ARP table with forged IP-to-MAC mappings, diverting traffic to the attacker.

questions.question: In a cluttered server room full of tangled cables, which tool helps trace which cable is which?
questions.why: A toner injects a signal into one cable so it can be traced and identified at the other end.

questions.question: Which device watches traffic and alerts on signature-matched threats but cannot react on its own?
questions.why: An IDS monitors and alerts but does not block; reacting automatically is the IPS's job.

questions.question: A new public web server must accept inbound port 80 from the internet and have no connections from the internal network. The firewall is triple-homed with PUBLIC, DMZ and PRIVATE zones. Where does the server go and how is the rule set?

choices.text: In the DMZ, with an inbound rule from eth0 to eth1 allowing port 80
In the DMZ, with an inbound rule from eth1 to eth0 allowing port 80
In the PUBLIC zone, with an inbound rule from eth0 to eth1 allowing port 80
In the PRIVATE zone, with an inbound rule from eth0 to eth1 allowing port 80

questions.correctText: In the DMZ, with an inbound rule from eth0 to eth1 allowing port 80
questions.why: Internet-facing servers sit in the DMZ; the rule lets outside traffic (eth0) reach the DMZ (eth1) on port 80 while the private zone stays isolated.

questions.question: Which protocol is typically used for centralized authentication and directory services that manage user credentials?
questions.why: LDAP is the standard protocol for directory services and centralized credential management.

questions.question: An 802.11g network suffers collisions and interference with access points sitting on channels 1, 5 and 11. Which channel reduces collisions?
questions.why: On 2.4 GHz only channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap; channel 5 overlaps its neighbors.

questions.question: On an OSPF network the internet-facing interface is congested, with traffic queued and slow, and the show interface output is provided. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Change the duplex setting from half to full
Assign a public IP address to the interface
Change the CIDR notation to a classful subnet mask

questions.correctText: Change the duplex setting from half to full
questions.why: The output shows half-duplex operation, which limits throughput and builds queues; full duplex lets the interface send and receive at once.

questions.question: Which attack can sit between two parties, intercept their traffic and change the data in transit?
questions.why: An on-path (man-in-the-middle) attack intercepts communication and can alter what passes through.

questions.question: After cutting a UTP cable from the spool, which tool removes its outer insulation before it is connected at the back of the patch panel?
questions.why: A cable stripper removes the outer sheath without nicking the conductors inside.

questions.question: Which technology lets IPv6-only clients talk to IPv4 servers?
questions.why: NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4 so v6-only devices can reach v4 resources.

questions.question: A user is on the company network with the correct SSID but cannot open any internet pages. What is the most likely cause?
questions.why: A wrong default gateway strands the user on the local network; nothing external can be reached.

questions.question: Which agreement, legally binding on those who sign it, is used to protect an organization's intellectual property?
questions.why: An NDA legally binds signatories to keep confidential information and IP from being disclosed.

questions.question: What must be in place so a technician can swap in replacement switches and get connectivity back quickly?
questions.why: With a configuration backup, the same settings can be loaded onto the replacement switch to restore service fast.

questions.question: Which document shows the network's cabling drawn over a floor plan?
questions.why: A physical network diagram maps the actual components and cabling against the building layout.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address for host 205.12.35.26/27?
questions.why: A /27 makes blocks of 32 addresses; .26 sits in the .0–.31 block, whose last address, .31, is the broadcast.

questions.question: Which metric describes the theoretical maximum rate at which data can be transferred?
questions.why: Bandwidth is the theoretical ceiling; throughput is what is actually achieved.

questions.question: A network sits in an industrial area where heavy machinery creates strong electromagnetic interference. Which cable type is best?
questions.why: Fiber sends light rather than electrical signals, so EMI cannot disturb it.

questions.question: Which metric states the maximum amount of data loss an organization can accept in a disaster recovery situation?
questions.why: The recovery point objective (RPO) defines how much data loss is tolerable, measured back in time.

questions.question: A web application needs to connect to a Microsoft SQL Server database. Which port does it use?
questions.why: Microsoft SQL Server listens on 1433 by default (3389 is RDP, 1521 Oracle, 3306 MySQL).

questions.question: A penetration test finds that a software bug could let an attacker read TLS traffic. What is the best mitigation?

choices.text: Install an IDS on the network

questions.why: The bug is the root cause, and a patch is what removes a known software flaw.

questions.question: Which system lets an organization control and manage user identities and their access to resources?
questions.why: Identity and access management (IAM) is built to manage identities and what they may access.

questions.question: Which of these network devices operates at Layer 2 of the OSI model?
questions.why: A switch works at Layer 2 and forwards frames by MAC address; routers are Layer 3 and repeaters Layer 1.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of link aggregation on a switch?

choices.text: Shrink broadcast domains by combining VLANs
Encrypt traffic across several physical links
Spread traffic evenly across every path
Combine several physical links into one faster logical link

questions.correctText: Combine several physical links into one faster logical link
questions.why: Link aggregation bundles multiple physical links into a single logical link with more bandwidth, plus redundancy.

questions.question: Which ports does SIP use?
questions.why: SIP signaling uses 5060, and 5061 when secured with TLS.

questions.question: A company is moving its headquarters and data center to Florida and is worried about hurricanes. Which long-term strategy document should it create?
questions.why: A business continuity plan keeps the whole business running during and after a disruption; it is broader than an IT-focused disaster recovery plan.

questions.question: In a three-tier datacenter architecture, which of these is NOT one of the tiers?
questions.why: The three tiers are core, distribution/aggregation and access/edge; a control layer belongs to SDN.

questions.question: What would you expect to see in the output of the show power command?

choices.text: A summary of routing protocols and their statuses
Power supply status, redundancy and health
Power consumption and status of the PoE ports
Power management settings for the interfaces

questions.correctText: Power consumption and status of the PoE ports
questions.why: show power reports how much power the PoE ports are drawing and their status.

questions.question: A user browses to a training company's website and is redirected to a malicious site instead. What attack most likely happened?
questions.why: DNS poisoning corrupts name resolution so a real domain points at the attacker's address.

questions.question: How many broadcast domains does a single 24-port switch form by itself?
questions.why: One switch is a single broadcast domain; its ports are separate collision domains, and VLANs or routers are needed to split broadcasts.

questions.question: An internet-facing FTP server sits on the internal network near the domain controller. How should the design change so a compromise of that server cannot reach internal systems?

choices.text: Make the firewall end with an implicit deny statement
Add a rule denying port 21 outbound
Upgrade the FTP server to SFTP
Move the FTP server into a screened subnet

questions.correctText: Move the FTP server into a screened subnet
questions.why: A screened subnet (DMZ) isolates public-facing servers from the LAN, so a breach stops at the perimeter.

questions.question: Before estimating how many wireless access points a network needs, what should an engineer consult?
questions.why: A site survey shows the physical space, obstacles and interference that drive AP count and placement.

questions.question: An old laptop with an 802.11b card cannot see the SSID of an 802.11g network. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: The router has no DHCP support configured
SSID broadcast is turned off on the router
The router is using WPA2 encryption

questions.correctText: SSID broadcast is turned off on the router
questions.why: If SSID broadcast is disabled the network name never appears in scans; 802.11b and g share 2.4 GHz and interoperate.

questions.question: Which wireless technology uses MU-MIMO over non-overlapping channels to raise throughput?
questions.why: 802.11ac brought in MU-MIMO, letting an AP talk to several clients at the same time.

questions.question: Which topology fits when every device must connect directly to every other device?
questions.why: A mesh links each device to all the others, giving many redundant paths.

questions.question: At a coffee shop, a customer unknowingly connects to a rogue access point pretending to be the shop's Wi-Fi. What is this attack called?
questions.why: An evil twin is a fake AP with a convincing name, set up to lure users into connecting.

questions.question: Which metric is the actual measured amount of data transferred?
questions.why: Throughput is the real, measured transfer rate; bandwidth is only the theoretical maximum.

questions.question: A switch-to-server link was designed for 10 Gbps but negotiates at 1 Gbps with default port settings. What is the fix?

choices.text: Manually set the switch port speed to 10 Gbps
Set the switch port to full-duplex
Enable jumbo frames on the port

questions.correctText: Manually set the switch port speed to 10 Gbps
questions.why: Hard-setting the port to 10 Gbps makes the link run at its designed speed instead of the negotiated fallback.

questions.question: A company wants a SaaS-style solution while keeping its sensitive data isolated from other customers. Which cloud type fits?
questions.why: A private cloud is dedicated to one organization, so its data stays separate from other tenants.

questions.question: Why is a route with a longer prefix length preferred over one with a shorter prefix?

choices.text: It is a more specific route to the destination

questions.correctText: It is a more specific route to the destination
questions.why: Routers prefer the longest matching prefix because it is the most specific route to the destination.

questions.question: A 10 Gbps multimode fiber link using 10GBaseLR transceivers fails at 450 meters. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The wrong transceivers are being used

questions.correctText: The wrong transceivers are being used
questions.why: 10GBaseLR optics are made for single-mode fiber; multimode needs 10GBaseSR, so the transceivers and fiber are mismatched (and fiber ignores EMI anyway).

questions.question: Which feature stops an attacker from changing the MAC-to-IP bindings in the ARP table?
questions.why: Dynamic ARP Inspection checks ARP packets against trusted IP-to-MAC bindings and drops forgeries.

questions.question: One employee orders inventory and a different employee must be the one to receive it. Which personnel control is this?
questions.why: Separation of duties splits a sensitive process between people so no one person can abuse it end to end.

questions.question: A Cat 5e run must go through a drop ceiling with no trays, near fluorescent lighting. Which cable type is the right choice?
questions.why: Shielded twisted pair resists the electrical interference that fluorescent lights can induce in a ceiling run.

questions.question: You installed a new NIC and want to test it by pinging the IPv4 loopback address. Which address do you ping?
questions.why: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address, used to test the local TCP/IP stack and NIC.

questions.question: Which approach is commonly used to let guests and employees bring personal devices onto the organization's network?
questions.why: A BYOD program allows personal devices onto the network under the organization's policies and controls.

questions.question: In cooling systems, what does port-side intake/exhaust refer to?

choices.text: The direction power supply fans push heat out of a server
How equipment and racks are oriented so airflow and cooling stay efficient
Software a server uses to regulate its own temperature
Switch settings that reduce electromagnetic interference

questions.correctText: How equipment and racks are oriented so airflow and cooling stay efficient
questions.why: Port-side intake/exhaust describes which side of the gear air enters and leaves, so racks must line up with the room's hot/cold aisle airflow.

questions.question: A cable in use turns out to have a single copper conductor wrapped in insulation and a metallic shield. What cable type is it?
questions.why: One central conductor, insulation and a metallic shield is exactly how coaxial cable is built.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address for host 189.76.60.164/26?
questions.why: A /26 makes blocks of 64; .164 falls in .128–.191, and the block's last address, .191, is the broadcast.

questions.question: Wireless users report speed and performance problems that began after AP2 was replaced (the floor plan shows AP1, AP2, AP3 and SW1). Changing as little as possible, which device do you log into first?
questions.why: The problems started with the AP2 replacement, so the new AP2 is the prime suspect and the first place to look.

questions.question: An internet-facing electronic sign with a public IP was digitally vandalized. What most likely let the attackers change its display?

choices.text: Unnecessary services were left enabled at install time
The default port 80 was left open at install time
The default credentials were never changed at install time

questions.correctText: The default credentials were never changed at install time
questions.why: Known factory-default logins on an internet-exposed device let anyone sign in and alter it.

questions.question: Which cloud connectivity option gives an organization a dedicated, private link between its data center and the cloud?
questions.why: Direct Connect provides a private, dedicated path into the cloud that avoids the public internet.

questions.question: Which TCP flag is used to politely request that a connection between two hosts be terminated?
questions.why: FIN asks for an orderly close; SYN opens a connection, RST kills it abruptly, and ACK acknowledges data.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a screened subnet to a network design?

choices.text: To act as a buffer zone between the internal network and the internet for public-facing services
To raise bandwidth by spreading traffic across subnets
To give new applications an isolated test environment
To store backups in a secure area away from the main network

questions.correctText: To act as a buffer zone between the internal network and the internet for public-facing services
questions.why: A screened subnet (DMZ) hosts internet-facing services in a buffer so a compromised server does not expose the LAN.

questions.question: Which statement about playbooks and templates in networking is true?

choices.text: They serve different purposes, but both are used to automate network configurations
Playbooks automate configurations while templates document network designs
They are interchangeable terms for the same thing
Playbooks document designs while templates automate configurations

questions.correctText: They serve different purposes, but both are used to automate network configurations
questions.why: Playbooks run sets of tasks and templates supply reusable configuration patterns — different roles, both about automation.

questions.question: Which Wi-Fi security protocol improves on its predecessor with better resistance to offline dictionary attacks and stronger encryption?
questions.why: WPA3 uses SAE in place of the older handshake, which resists offline dictionary attacks and strengthens encryption.

questions.question: A switch connecting workstations has failed. What is the quickest way to get a replacement switch configured?
questions.why: Restoring a saved switch image (its full configuration) onto the replacement is faster than rebuilding settings by hand.

questions.question: What error is reported when a switch receives an Ethernet frame smaller than 64 bytes?
questions.why: Undersized frames under 64 bytes are called runts; oversized ones are giants, and a CRC error means a checksum mismatch.

questions.question: Which mechanism gives proactive notification of network events for efficient monitoring and troubleshooting?
questions.why: SNMP traps push event notifications to a manager, enabling proactive monitoring and troubleshooting.

questions.question: Which DNS record type supports reverse lookups, mapping an IP address back to a domain name?
questions.why: A PTR record points an IP address to a hostname for reverse DNS; AAAA is a forward IPv6 mapping, CNAME an alias, NS a nameserver.

questions.question: A gigabit link between a switch and a server carries large transfers in both directions at once. Which duplex setting is most efficient?

choices.text: Full-duplex, so both sides can send and receive simultaneously
Auto-negotiation that switches between half and full duplex

questions.correctText: Full-duplex, so both sides can send and receive simultaneously
questions.why: Full duplex lets both ends transmit and receive at the same time, maximizing two-way throughput.

questions.question: An organization needs a recovery site it can shift operations to and keep the business running immediately. Which site type is that?
questions.why: A hot site mirrors the live environment and is ready to take over at once; warm and cold sites need setup time first.

questions.question: What security capability does SNMPv3 add that earlier SNMP versions lacked?
questions.why: SNMPv3 secures management traffic with authentication and encryption instead of relying on plain community strings.
questions.whyWrong: Discovery, speed and VLAN support are not SNMPv3 security features; earlier versions already handled queries and VLAN data without protection.

questions.question: Which control lets only one person pass into or out of a server room at a time?
questions.why: An access control vestibule (mantrap) forces one door to close before the other opens, so only one person passes at a time and tailgating is blocked.
questions.whyWrong: A cipher lock or thumbprint reader authenticates but does not physically enforce one-at-a-time passage; cameras only record what happens.

questions.question: New Ethernet cabling was installed in an office and users now have intermittent connectivity. What is the most likely cabling fault?
questions.why: Poorly crimped or incorrectly wired terminations are the classic cause of flaky connections right after an install.
questions.whyWrong: Crosstalk, length problems and jacket damage are possible but far less common than bad terminations on fresh cabling.

questions.question: Which port is used for secure remote sessions over the internet?
questions.why: SSH runs on port 22 and encrypts the session.
questions.whyWrong: Port 23 is Telnet (unencrypted), 80 is HTTP, and 25 is SMTP mail.

questions.question: Why is it important to track warranty support for network hardware?

choices.text: To monitor traffic and detect threats
To keep device software up to date
To follow the support lifecycle and plan replacement schedules
To protect devices and manage user access

questions.correctText: To follow the support lifecycle and plan replacement schedules
questions.why: Warranty tracking shows when support ends, so replacements can be planned before coverage lapses.
questions.whyWrong: Traffic monitoring, software updates and access control are separate operational tasks, not what warranty tracking is for.

questions.question: What does configuration drift mean?

choices.text: A gradual move away from the intended configuration
A deliberate change made for performance

questions.correctText: A gradual move away from the intended configuration
questions.why: Drift is the slow, unintentional divergence of a device's actual settings from its intended baseline.
questions.whyWrong: Synchronization, intentional tuning and backups are planned activities, not unintended deviation.

questions.question: Which authentication method uses an RFID chip to open a locked room?
questions.why: A proximity badge carries an RFID chip that a reader scans to authenticate the holder.
questions.whyWrong: A vestibule is a physical layout, a biometric reader scans body traits, and CCTV only watches.

questions.question: Which scenario is the best fit for SD-WAN?

choices.text: A multinational company with branches worldwide that needs centralized management
A home network with a few devices

questions.correctText: A multinational company with branches worldwide that needs centralized management
questions.why: SD-WAN shines in large, distributed organizations that need central control over policies across many WAN links.
questions.whyWrong: Small single-site networks gain little from SD-WAN's centralized multi-link management.

questions.question: In a large all-Cisco enterprise network, which protocol discovers directly connected neighboring devices?
questions.why: CDP is Cisco's own discovery protocol and shares neighbor, interface and management details; LLDP is the vendor-neutral counterpart.
questions.whyWrong: STP prevents loops, SNMP manages devices, and LLDP is not Cisco-specific.

questions.question: Why does maintaining proper temperature matter in a physical network installation?
questions.why: Heat swings and overheating make hardware malfunction or fail early, hurting reliability.
questions.whyWrong: Comfort, energy cost and speed are side effects, not the reason temperature control protects the installation.

questions.question: You tested a theory of probable cause and it was not confirmed. What do you do next?

choices.text: Establish a new theory or escalate
Go back to identifying the problem

questions.correctText: Establish a new theory or escalate
questions.why: When a theory fails testing, you form a new theory of probable cause — or escalate if you are out of ideas.
questions.whyWrong: Jumping straight to escalation skips forming a new theory; preventive measures and re-identification are not the next methodology step here.

questions.question: Which tool pinpoints the exact location of a break in single-mode fiber?
questions.why: An OTDR fires light pulses down the fiber and times the reflections to locate a fault's distance.
questions.whyWrong: A light meter only measures power, a media converter changes media types, and a tone generator is for copper.

questions.question: A T1 circuit has connectivity problems and everything else has been verified. Which tool helps isolate the fault?
questions.why: A loopback adapter sends the transmit signal back into the receiver, testing the local interface and separating a local fault from a line fault.
questions.whyWrong: Tone generators trace copper pairs, cable testers check cabling, and a light meter is for fiber — none loop a T1 interface back on itself.

questions.question: Which DNS record type specifies the host and port for services such as instant messaging?
questions.why: An SRV record names the host and port (with priority and weight) that provide a service.
questions.whyWrong: TXT holds text data, PTR is for reverse lookups, and SOA describes the zone's authority.

questions.question: You are making Cat 7 patch cables, and the patch panel and wall jacks are already installed and tested. Which tool is NOT needed?
questions.why: A punchdown tool terminates cable onto patch panels and blocks — those are already done, so only stripping, crimping and testing remain.
questions.whyWrong: The stripper, crimper and tester are all used when building and verifying patch cables.

questions.question: Which DNS record maps a domain name to an IPv4 address?
questions.why: The A record ties a hostname to its IPv4 address.
questions.whyWrong: AAAA is the IPv6 version, MX routes mail, and SOA holds zone authority data.

questions.question: Which DHCP feature hands clients extra settings such as DNS server addresses along with the lease?
questions.why: DHCP Options carry the additional parameters (DNS servers, gateway, and so on) delivered with an address.
questions.whyWrong: A scope is the address pool, reservations pin addresses to MACs, and a relay forwards requests — none of them are the extra-settings mechanism.

questions.question: Which attack corrupts name resolution so web traffic is redirected and sensitive information can be stolen?
questions.why: DNS poisoning plants false entries in a DNS cache, sending users to malicious sites where data can be intercepted.
questions.whyWrong: SSL stripping downgrades HTTPS connections, and ARP spoofing works on the local segment's ARP table rather than the DNS cache.

questions.question: A disgruntled employee installs a keylogger on team workstations and harvests credentials. How is this threat classified?
questions.why: A trusted insider abusing legitimate access to harm the organization is an insider threat.
questions.whyWrong: There is no delayed trigger (logic bomb), no service outage goal (DoS), and no one was tricked (social engineering).

questions.question: Two workstations with dynamic addresses ended up with duplicate IP addresses. Which command sequence fixes it?
questions.why: Releasing first gives up the conflicting lease; renewing then pulls a fresh, unique address from DHCP.
questions.whyWrong: Renewing alone may hand back the same conflicting address, /all only displays settings, and /dhcp is not the fix.

questions.question: Coffee-shop Wi-Fi sends every new user to a web page before granting access. What technology is that?
questions.why: A captive portal intercepts the first connection and redirects the user to a login or terms page.
questions.whyWrong: Encryption, MAC filtering and SSID broadcast do not produce a redirect page.

questions.question: Which plan sets out how an organization responds to an unplanned event or outage and keeps operating?
questions.why: A business continuity plan describes how the business keeps running during and after a disruption.
questions.whyWrong: A disaster recovery plan focuses on restoring IT systems, and an incident response plan is for security incidents specifically.

questions.question: Which approach integrates IPv4 and IPv6 seamlessly while keeping backward compatibility?
questions.why: Dual stack runs IPv4 and IPv6 side by side on the same devices, so both worlds interoperate during migration.
questions.whyWrong: Tunneling wraps one protocol inside another, NAT traversal solves NAT passage, and SLAAC only auto-assigns IPv6 addresses.

questions.question: Transmissions are frequently delayed and incomplete, with packets failing to reach their destination. What condition is this?
questions.why: Packets that never arrive are packet loss; the gaps force retransmissions and incomplete transfers.
questions.whyWrong: Latency is delay itself and jitter is variation in delay — neither describes packets going missing.

questions.question: Two routers share a point-to-point /30 link that includes the address 77.81.12.13. What is the link's broadcast address?
questions.why: In the /30 block .12–.15, .12 is the network address and the last address, .15, is the broadcast; .13 and .14 are the usable hosts.
questions.whyWrong: .12 is the network address of the block, and .13/.14 are the two usable host addresses — none of them is the broadcast.

questions.question: A VoIP call sounds choppy, speeding up and slowing down. Which condition causes that?
questions.why: Jitter is uneven packet arrival timing; when voice packets bunch up or lag, speech speeds up, slows down and sounds choppy.
questions.whyWrong: Bandwidth and throughput are capacity measures, and steady latency delays everything evenly instead of distorting it.

questions.question: Which plan provides the framework for reacting to an incident such as a malware outbreak?
questions.why: An incident response plan lays out how to detect, respond to and recover from security incidents.
questions.whyWrong: BYOD and AUP are usage policies, and a life cycle plan covers an asset's lifespan — none guide incident handling.

questions.question: Which remote access tool provides command-line terminal emulation over TCP port 23?
questions.why: Telnet is the classic unencrypted remote terminal protocol on port 23; SSH on 22 is its secure replacement.
questions.whyWrong: RDP and VNC are graphical remote desktop tools, and SSH uses port 22 with encryption.

questions.question: A VoIP phone on voice VLAN 150 works fine, but the PC plugged in behind it on data VLAN 100 gets no connectivity. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: VLAN 100 is not configured on the switch
The switch port is not trunked properly
The native VLAN is mismatched on the switch port
The phone is incompatible with the switch's VLAN setup

questions.correctText: The native VLAN is mismatched on the switch port
questions.why: The PC's data traffic is untagged and rides the native/access VLAN; when that mismatches, data is stranded while the tagged voice VLAN still works.
questions.whyWrong: If VLAN 100 were missing entirely or the phone incompatible, the failure pattern would differ; the tagged voice path passing points at the native VLAN.

questions.question: Which standard sets the requirements for handling credit card data securely?
questions.why: PCI DSS is the standard written specifically to protect cardholder and payment data.
questions.whyWrong: HIPAA covers health data, GDPR covers personal data privacy in general, and ISO 27001 is a broad security management framework.

questions.question: A switch has two paths to the root bridge. What STP state is the redundant port in?
questions.why: STP blocks the higher-cost redundant port so Layer 2 loops cannot form, while the best path keeps forwarding.
questions.whyWrong: Forwarding, learning and listening are states of ports on active paths, not of the parked redundant port.

questions.question: You need to reach a Linux server 50 miles away that runs unencrypted VNC. How do you connect securely?
questions.why: Tunneling the VNC session through SSH wraps the unencrypted traffic in an encrypted channel end to end.
questions.whyWrong: WPA2 protects local Wi-Fi, HTTPS secures web traffic, and plain RDP does not encrypt this VNC session.

questions.question: Which syslog severity level corresponds to a debugging condition?
questions.why: Syslog severities run from 0 (emergency, most severe) down to 7, which is debug — the least severe.
questions.whyWrong: Levels 0 and 1 are emergency and alert, and 6 is informational — all more severe than debug.

questions.question: Which device is used to separate collision domains?
questions.why: A bridge forwards at Layer 2 and places each segment in its own collision domain.
questions.whyWrong: A hub puts everything in one shared collision domain; access points and media converters do not segment collisions.

questions.question: Three 802.11a devices are being connected to an 802.11g access point that uses WEP. What is the problem?
questions.why: 802.11a runs on 5 GHz and 802.11g on 2.4 GHz, so the devices cannot hear each other at all.
questions.whyWrong: Both sides use WEP here, and interference or weak signal cannot explain total incompatibility across bands.

questions.question: What is the core difference between a trusted and an untrusted network?

choices.text: Trusted networks encrypt everything; untrusted ones use plaintext
Trusted networks are inside the company firewall; untrusted ones are outside and not governed by its policies
Trusted networks need extra authentication; untrusted ones are unrestricted
Trusted networks are external and share sensitive data; untrusted ones are internal

questions.correctText: Trusted networks are inside the company firewall; untrusted ones are outside and not governed by its policies
questions.why: Trusted networks live inside the firewall under the organization's control; untrusted networks, like the internet, sit outside that control.
questions.whyWrong: Encryption and authentication choices vary on both sides; the defining line is the firewall boundary and policy control.

questions.question: A single central server manages credentials for all network devices. Which service is that?
questions.why: RADIUS centralizes authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA) for network device and user access.
questions.whyWrong: DNS resolves names, FTP moves files, and Kerberos is a ticket-based authentication protocol rather than the device-access AAA service described.

questions.question: A department subnet must support 32 devices. Which CIDR notation is the right fit?
questions.why: 32 devices plus the network and broadcast addresses need at least 34 addresses; a /26 provides 64 total (62 usable).
questions.whyWrong: Smaller blocks like /27, /28, /29 and /30 do not have enough addresses, and a /25 wastes far more than needed.

questions.question: Which command verifies the MAC addresses a switch has learned?
questions.why: show mac-address-table lists the learned MAC-to-port and VLAN mappings.
questions.whyWrong: show arp shows IP-to-MAC mappings, and the interface commands show link status rather than the learned MAC table.

questions.question: Which protocol synchronizes clocks between computer systems over a network?
questions.why: NTP keeps system clocks aligned, which logs, authentication and schedules all depend on.
questions.whyWrong: DNS resolves names, TFTP transfers files, and DHCP assigns addresses — none discipline clocks.

questions.question: Which wireless standard uses both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz with speeds from about 108 up to 600 Mbps?
questions.why: 802.11n is dual-band and, with MIMO, reaches up to 600 Mbps.
questions.whyWrong: 802.11ac is 5 GHz only and faster; a, b and g are single-band and slower.

questions.question: Which attack is a non-technical trick that pressures a user into handing over sensitive information?
questions.why: Social engineering manipulates people rather than technology to extract confidential information.
questions.whyWrong: Bluesnarfing, on-path attacks and evil twins are technical attacks on devices or traffic.

questions.question: Which metric does OSPF use to select routes?
questions.why: OSPF picks the path with the lowest total cost, a value derived from link bandwidth.
questions.whyWrong: Hop count is RIP's metric; raw bandwidth and load are inputs or unrelated measures, not OSPF's decision value.

questions.question: Which device separates broadcast domains?
questions.why: Routers do not forward broadcasts, so each router interface bounds a separate broadcast domain.
questions.whyWrong: Switches, bridges and hubs all forward broadcasts within one domain (a hub is the plainest case).

questions.question: Which device can separate broadcast domains? (same idea, different choices)
questions.why: A multilayer (Layer 3) switch routes between VLANs like a router, so each VLAN is its own broadcast domain.
questions.whyWrong: Plain bridges, hubs and media converters keep everything in a single broadcast domain.

questions.question: In STP, what are blocking, listening, learning and forwarding?
questions.why: Per the site's revealed answer, these are the STP port roles/states a port moves through; STP works at Layer 2, not with IP addressing.
questions.whyWrong: They are not VLAN assignments, MAC addresses or IP addresses — STP operates below the IP layer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of static routing?

choices.text: To improve security by automatically rejecting unknown routes
To cut overhead by auto-discovering the best path
To manually configure routes that change only when edited by hand

questions.correctText: To manually configure routes that change only when edited by hand
questions.why: Static routes are entered by an administrator and never change on their own — predictable, but with no automatic failover.
questions.whyWrong: Automatic discovery, dynamic updates and auto-rejection describe dynamic behavior, the opposite of static routing.

questions.question: Which cloud characteristic lets many customers share the same physical resources while staying isolated from each other?
questions.why: Multi-tenancy uses virtualization to keep tenants isolated while they share the same underlying hardware.
questions.whyWrong: Scalability, redundancy and elasticity describe growth, duplication and flexible sizing — not shared-but-isolated hosting.

questions.question: A disgruntled employee redirects Layer 2 traffic meant for the gateway through his own machine. What attack is this?
questions.why: Forged ARP replies bind the gateway's IP address to the attacker's MAC, pulling traffic through the attacker.
questions.whyWrong: IP spoofing fakes source addresses, reflective DNS abuses resolvers for amplification, and an evil twin is a rogue access point.

questions.question: What does the dig command return for example.com?

choices.text: The IP address associated with example.com
A list of all active connections
The physical address of the hosting server

questions.correctText: The IP address associated with example.com
questions.why: dig queries DNS and returns the domain's records — here, the A record's IP address.
questions.whyWrong: Connection lists come from netstat-style tools, and dig reports neither bandwidth nor hardware addresses.

questions.question: Someone bought a domain and created an A record pointing it at an IP address. Which tool verifies the record?
questions.why: dig queries DNS directly, so it confirms whether the new A record resolves (allowing time for propagation).
questions.whyWrong: tcpdump captures packets, arp shows the local IP-to-MAC cache, and ipconfig shows local adapter settings — none query DNS records.

questions.question: A department subnet has 11 devices. Which CIDR notation is the most efficient fit?
questions.why: 11 devices plus network and broadcast need 13 addresses; a /28 gives 16 total and 14 usable — the smallest block that fits.
questions.whyWrong: A /29 offers only 6 usable addresses, and /25, /26 and /27 all waste more space than necessary.

questions.question: Which troubleshooting step involves identifying what changed in the network configuration before the problem appeared?

choices.text: Establish a theory of probable cause
Test the theory to determine the cause

questions.correctText: Establish a theory of probable cause
questions.why: Forming a theory of probable cause includes gathering information and spotting recent changes, which narrows the likely causes.
questions.whyWrong: Testing comes after the theory exists, implementing and escalating come later still, and documenting closes the process.

questions.question: Which fiber type is most commonly used for short-distance transmission on local networks?
questions.why: Multimode fiber is the cost-effective choice for short local runs, with a larger core suited to nearby links.
questions.whyWrong: Single-mode's smaller core targets long distances; twisted pair and coax are copper media, not fiber.

questions.question: NAC finds a virus on a client's laptop. Where should the laptop be placed for cleanup without endangering the network?
questions.why: A quarantine network isolates a non-compliant device until it is remediated and meets the entry requirements.
questions.whyWrong: A botnet is a herd of infected machines under an attacker's control, a DMZ hosts public services, and a honeypot is a decoy.

questions.question: Someone is setting up Wi-Fi for a large backyard that stretches out in one direction. Which antenna type fits best?
questions.why: A directional antenna focuses its signal toward the area that needs coverage, which matches a yard extending one way.
questions.whyWrong: Omnidirectional wastes signal in every direction; a parabolic is built for long point-to-point links rather than area coverage.

questions.question: A small office has many internal devices that need internet access, and public IP addresses must be conserved. Which NAT type should be used?
questions.why: PAT (NAT overload) lets many internal devices share one public address by separating their traffic with unique port numbers.
questions.whyWrong: Static NAT burns a public address per device, dynamic NAT draws from a pool, and proxy ARP is not a translation method.

questions.question: An administrator is upgrading server-room switches for 10 Gbps over the existing Cat 6a cabling. Which standard applies?
questions.why: 10GBaseT delivers 10 Gbps over twisted-pair copper, and Cat 6a supports it.
questions.whyWrong: The SW, FX and SR variants are fiber standards and cannot run on the installed Cat 6a.

questions.question: Which policy defines which types of VPN connections are allowed?
questions.why: A remote access policy sets out the approved ways of connecting to the internal network from outside, including VPN use.
questions.whyWrong: Password and DLP policies govern credentials and data handling, and an AUP states general usage rules.

questions.question: Why does managing software licensing matter to an organization?

choices.text: It keeps steady, uninterrupted power to recorded devices
It maintains the security of infrastructure and devices
It enables remote access to the same software offsite
It ensures software is used legally and avoids penalties for non-compliance

questions.correctText: It ensures software is used legally and avoids penalties for non-compliance
questions.why: License management proves the software in use is legal, avoiding fines and penalties for non-compliance.
questions.whyWrong: Power continuity, infrastructure security and remote access are separate concerns that licensing does not address.

questions.question: An audit finds employees using company laptops and desktops for personal use. Which document addresses this?
questions.why: The acceptable use policy spells out what employees may and may not do with company IT equipment.
questions.whyWrong: An MOU frames an agreement's scope, an SLA is a provider's service commitment, and an NDA protects shared confidential material.

questions.question: Fifty PoE cameras were deployed, and after installation some of them never power on. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Ethernet cables that are too long, causing power loss
The PoE switch's power budget has been exceeded
The cameras need a higher PoE standard than the switch supports

questions.correctText: The PoE switch's power budget has been exceeded
questions.why: When the total draw of all cameras passes what the switch can supply, the excess devices simply stay off — the classic power-budget symptom.
questions.whyWrong: If the switch were not PoE-capable or the standard were wrong, all cameras would fail alike; cable length within spec does not stop power-on.

questions.question: A network segment was just expanded and users now report intermittent connectivity. What should you check first?
questions.why: Duplicate addresses make traffic bounce unpredictably between the two devices sharing an address, which fits intermittent symptoms after an expansion.
questions.whyWrong: Port configuration faults tend to be all-or-nothing, and speed/duplex or PoE issues are less likely to come and go like this.

questions.question: Which command maps the Layer 3 hops a packet takes to a remote destination?
questions.why: Traceroute sends probes with increasing TTL values; each router that drops one replies, revealing every hop along the path.
questions.whyWrong: ping only tests end-to-end reachability, nslookup is for DNS, and netstat shows connection statistics.

questions.question: In SDN, which layer decides how a data packet should be routed?
questions.why: The control layer takes application information and makes the routing, prioritization and forwarding decisions.
questions.whyWrong: The application layer requests services, the infrastructure layer is the hardware that moves data, and the management plane oversees administration.

questions.question: What key benefit does network segmentation provide?
questions.why: Dividing the network into segments isolates them from each other, which contains breaches and improves security.
questions.whyWrong: Aggregation, mirroring and redundancy are separate features that segmentation by itself does not deliver.

questions.question: A telecom company is launching a high-speed service in a dense urban area. Which frequency band suits it best?
questions.why: 6 GHz adds fresh spectrum capacity with little interference, which suits high-speed service in crowded cities.
questions.whyWrong: 2.4 GHz is congested, 5 GHz still faces urban interference, and 60 GHz is very short-range with poor penetration.

questions.question: Why choose WPA3 over WPA2?

choices.text: WPA3 works with a wider range of devices
WPA3 provides stronger encryption and security

questions.correctText: WPA3 provides stronger encryption and security
questions.why: WPA3's value is its improved encryption and overall security over WPA2.
questions.whyWrong: WPA3 is newer, not older; it does not meaningfully change speeds, and device compatibility is narrower, not wider.

questions.question: Which remote access technology should NOT be used because it is insecure?
questions.why: Telnet sends everything — usernames, passwords, commands — in plaintext, wide open to sniffing.
questions.whyWrong: SSH encrypts its sessions, a VPN builds an encrypted tunnel, and RDP encrypts its traffic by design.

questions.question: A department subnet needs room for 13 devices. Which CIDR notation is the most efficient?
questions.why: 13 devices plus network and broadcast need 15 addresses; a /28 gives 16 total and 14 usable — the tightest fit.
questions.whyWrong: A /29 (6 usable) and /30 (2 usable) are too small, and /25, /26 and /27 overshoot the requirement.

questions.question: An administrator wants to define a VLAN once and have it propagate to every switch. What should be configured?

choices.text: Configure the switches to use STP
Configure the switches to use VTP
Configure the switches to use IGRP

questions.correctText: Configure the switches to use VTP
questions.why: VTP shares VLAN configuration across the domain, so defining it on the VTP server pushes it to all switches.
questions.whyWrong: STP prevents loops, bonding aggregates links, and IGRP exchanges routes — none distribute VLAN definitions.

questions.question: In cyber forensics, which document lists everywhere a piece of evidence has been?
questions.why: Chain-of-custody records track every change in control, handling and possession of evidence.
questions.whyWrong: A warrant authorizes a search, and a forensic report presents findings — neither is the running custody log.

questions.question: An administrator edits a firewall rule and suddenly no FTP user can reach the server. Which earlier action would have prevented this?
questions.why: A submitted and approved change request starts the process; notification, scheduling and documentation all follow from it.
questions.whyWrong: The other three are steps that happen after approval, so none of them is the first, preventive action.

questions.question: A failed router is replaced with the same model that sat in storage for 13 months, and HTTPS will not enable for remote access. What fixes it?
questions.why: A router shelved that long likely runs old firmware without working HTTPS; updating it adds the missing features and security patches.
questions.whyWrong: A reboot changes nothing about the firmware, a reset only restores defaults, and HTTP is an insecure step backwards.

questions.question: A small law office has three 8-port switches, one 4-port hub and one 2-port router: switch 1 connects to the router's Fa0/0, switches 2 and 3 hang off switch 1, and the hub connects to Fa0/1. How many broadcast domains are there?
questions.why: Routers split broadcast domains: everything behind Fa0/0 (the three switches) is one domain, and the hub behind Fa0/1 is the second.
questions.whyWrong: Counting switches or ports individually ignores that only the router's two sides create separate domains.

questions.question: Which plan dictates the response when a fire leaves the office building unusable for three months?
questions.why: A disaster recovery plan is the structured approach for resuming work quickly after an unplanned incident like a fire.
questions.whyWrong: A business continuity plan is the broader operations plan, an incident response plan targets security incidents, and a life cycle plan tracks an asset's lifespan.

questions.question: Which tool observes a signal's frequency as it is transmitted or received?
questions.why: A spectrum analyzer measures the magnitude of a signal across its frequencies.
questions.whyWrong: A TDR locates copper faults from reflections, a tone generator traces cable pairs, and a WiFi analyzer focuses on wireless networks rather than raw frequency.

questions.question: The goal is better cable management and fault isolation in the server room, with server connections easy to reach and identify. What should be installed?

choices.text: A patch panel for centralized cable management
A subnet mask to divide IP space

questions.correctText: A patch panel for centralized cable management
questions.why: A patch panel centralizes every connection in one labeled place, making identification and fault isolation fast.
questions.whyWrong: VLANs and subnet masks are logical tools, and colored cables alone give no central management point.

questions.question: Which form factor is typically associated with a single-channel data link in networking equipment?
questions.why: An SFP module typically carries a single-channel link, commonly 1 Gbps Ethernet.
questions.whyWrong: QSFP+ is built for higher-speed multi-lane links, and M.2 and USB are not single-channel network form factors.

questions.question: Fifteen local banks form a shared company to build one secure cloud environment that only the member banks can use. Which cloud model is it?
questions.why: A community cloud is shared by organizations from the same community with similar needs — here, the 15 member banks.
questions.whyWrong: A private cloud serves one organization, a public cloud serves anyone, and a hybrid mixes models rather than describing a members-only shared cloud.

questions.question: Which protocol is most often abused to steal email passwords with a network sniffer?
questions.why: Plain HTTP sends logins in clear text, so a sniffer can read webmail credentials straight off the wire.
questions.whyWrong: SSL encrypts traffic, TFTP moves config files, and DNS only resolves names — none carries email passwords in the clear.

questions.question: Warehouse workers scan packages as they arrive, using sensors that reach about 30 cm (1 ft). Which technology is this?
questions.why: RFID reads tags automatically at that range and is built for tracking items like incoming packages.
questions.whyWrong: NFC reaches only a few centimeters, Bluetooth is a personal-area link without warehouse coverage, and Wi-Fi provides network access rather than tag scanning.

questions.question: Which port does SMTP with TLS use?
questions.why: Port 587 is the standard submission port for SMTP with TLS.
questions.whyWrong: Port 25 is plain SMTP relay, 993 is IMAP over SSL, and 995 is POP3 over SSL.

questions.question: A new office network connects Gigabit Ethernet devices. Which cable type is the LEAST suitable?
questions.why: Plain Cat 5 has the least bandwidth and the weakest crosstalk protection, making it the unreliable choice for gigabit.
questions.whyWrong: Cat 5e, Cat 6 and Cat 6a were all designed to carry gigabit and beyond consistently.

questions.question: Which tool identifies why an 802.11g network keeps dropping traffic intermittently?
questions.why: A WiFi analyzer shows signal strength, channels in use and RF interference, exposing dead zones or interference behind the drops.
questions.whyWrong: The other tools test wired cabling or electrical values and cannot see wireless conditions.

questions.question: Which of these is a classless routing protocol?
questions.why: OSPF carries subnet masks in its updates, so it supports VLSM and exact network boundaries — the definition of classless.
questions.whyWrong: RIPv1 and IGRP are classful and never send mask information; STP is a Layer 2 loop-prevention protocol, not routing at all.

questions.question: Which tool is most effective for checking a wireless signal's strength, channel use and interference?
questions.why: A WiFi analyzer is purpose-built to scan wireless networks and report signal strength, channel usage and interference.
questions.whyWrong: Cable testers and multimeters are wired tools, and a general spectrum analyzer is not tailored to Wi-Fi analysis.

questions.question: A switch port is inactive because it is not on the best path to the root bridge. What state is it in?
questions.why: In STP, a port left off the best path stays blocking — it forwards nothing but still listens for BPDUs to guard against loops.
questions.whyWrong: Listening is a brief transitional state, and idle and standby are not STP states at all.

questions.question: Which wireless characteristic does channel bonding improve?
questions.why: Channel bonding joins two adjacent channels into one wider channel, raising throughput between devices.
questions.whyWrong: It does not change transmit power (signal strength), the area covered, or the encryption in use.

questions.question: A routing protocol is not picking the shortest path to a destination, and you want the most efficient routes chosen. What do you adjust?

choices.text: Adjust the metric value to steer path selection toward the efficient route
Change the prefix length to make a route look more specific
Configure ACLs to push traffic down the preferred path
Alter administrative distance to prefer one protocol's routes

questions.correctText: Adjust the metric value to steer path selection toward the efficient route
questions.why: The metric is the value a protocol uses to rank paths, so tuning it directly steers selection toward the efficient route.
questions.whyWrong: Administrative distance only arbitrates between different protocols, ACLs enforce policy rather than path choice, and prefix length changes specificity, not efficiency.

questions.question: Brownouts keep making a router lose power and reboot. What should be installed to stop that?
questions.why: A UPS supplies battery power and smooths the supply during drops, so the router stays up instead of power-cycling.
questions.whyWrong: A new outlet is electrician work and does not fix an unstable feed; a surge protector guards against spikes, not drops, and a newer router would still lose power.

questions.question: Fast Ethernet devices need high-speed internet and VoIP. What switch port setting fits?
questions.why: Fast Ethernet is 100 Mbps, and full-duplex lets a port send and receive at the same time.
questions.whyWrong: 10 Mbps wastes the devices' capability, half-duplex gigabit does not match Fast Ethernet, and auto-negotiation can settle on poor settings if it fails.

questions.question: RADIUS AAA is set up, but users can only log in locally and remote authentication fails. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The RADIUS shared secret is incorrect
The username was not added to the RADIUS server
Group policy changes have not propagated
The local firewall is blocking LDAP traffic

questions.correctText: The RADIUS shared secret is incorrect
questions.why: The client and server must share the same secret to talk securely; a mismatch breaks the whole authentication exchange.
questions.whyWrong: A missing username would fail one user, not everyone; LDAP is not used by RADIUS here, and group policy is unrelated to the RADIUS handshake.

questions.question: What is the network ID for host 172.16.200.130/26?
questions.why: A /26 block holds 64 addresses, and .130 sits in the block that starts at .128.
questions.whyWrong: The other choices are outside that block or are host/broadcast-style addresses, not the first address of the .128 block.

questions.question: A newly installed WAP drops connections sporadically. What should be checked first?
questions.why: Poor placement lets walls and building materials weaken the signal; a site survey confirms coverage.
questions.whyWrong: The SSID or encryption type would block connections outright rather than drop them at random, and saturation slows traffic instead of dropping it.

questions.question: A patch cable tests fine. What best helps identify which switch port connects to a given wall jack?
questions.why: Labels on cables, jacks and patch panels let you trace a run to its switch port at a glance.
questions.whyWrong: A baseline measures performance, procedures describe routine steps, and inventory tracks stock - none of them identify a specific port.

questions.question: In nslookup interactive mode, which command shows a domain's name servers?
questions.why: The set type=ns command tells nslookup to return only NS records.
questions.whyWrong: Locate, request and transfer are not valid nslookup interactive commands.

questions.question: An engineer disabled a switch port for a firewall install; afterward the firewall cannot connect. What is most likely?

choices.text: The port error-disabled from excessive CRC errors
The port is still administratively down
The firewall is incompatible with the switch OS version
The firewall's MAC was not added to the MAC table

questions.correctText: The port is still administratively down
questions.why: A manually shut port stays down until someone re-enables it, so nothing connected to it can link.
questions.whyWrong: Error-disable comes from faults like CRC storms, OS version issues affect management rather than the link, and switches learn MACs automatically.

questions.question: Which command shows all established connections and listening ports on a server?
questions.why: netstat lists active connections, listening ports, routing tables and interface stats.
questions.whyWrong: dig queries DNS, ipconfig shows local IP settings, and arp only shows the IP-to-MAC cache.

questions.question: A cable test report shows pass/fail with open and short readings for a Cat 5e cable. Which tool made it?
questions.why: A certifier verifies a cable against its spec and reports pass/fail plus faults like opens, shorts and length.
questions.whyWrong: A crimper attaches connectors, a punchdown tool seats wires in blocks, a multimeter reads electrical values, a protocol analyzer watches traffic, and an OTDR is for fiber.

questions.question: Which command sends ICMP echo requests to test reachability and measure round-trip time?
questions.why: ping sends ICMP echo requests and reports replies and round-trip time.
questions.whyWrong: Traceroute maps the path, nslookup queries DNS, and tcpdump captures packets.

questions.question: One department is slow, worst during video conferences; hardware and configuration check out. What is most likely?

choices.text: Congestion from increased video conferencing traffic at peak hours
A firewall misconfiguration blocking the department's subnet
Incorrect VLAN settings on switch ports to access points

questions.correctText: Congestion from increased video conferencing traffic at peak hours
questions.why: Heavy video traffic at peak times congests the links; QoS or more bandwidth is the fix.
questions.whyWrong: VLAN or firewall faults would block traffic rather than slow it, and slow DNS would delay websites, not video calls.

questions.question: Which command checks IP configuration and DHCP settings on Ubuntu workstations with intermittent connectivity?
questions.why: ifconfig on Linux shows interface addresses, masks and gateways.
questions.whyWrong: ipconfig is the Windows equivalent, netstat shows connections and stats, and nslookup is for DNS.

questions.question: What collects logs from many devices across the network so events can be correlated?
questions.why: A syslog server centralizes log collection, making correlation and alerting much easier.
questions.whyWrong: DNS resolves names, DHCP assigns addresses, and a proxy sits between clients and servers - none gather device logs.

questions.question: Which mask splits 192.168.0.0/24 into exactly 4 equal subnets?
questions.why: 255.255.255.192 is /26, which quarters the /24 into four blocks of 64 addresses.
questions.whyWrong: /25 makes only 2 subnets, while /27 and /28 make 8 and 16 - more than asked.

questions.question: Which media converter connects a new RG-6 coax run to an existing single-mode fiber plant?
questions.why: A media converter changes one physical media type to another - here coax to fiber.
questions.whyWrong: The link starts as coax and ends as fiber, so ethernet or multimode conversions do not describe it.

questions.question: Which electrical characteristic is the potential difference between two points in a circuit?
questions.why: Voltage is defined as the potential difference between two points.
questions.whyWrong: Current is charge flow, resistance opposes that flow, and power factor describes how efficiently power is used.

questions.question: A SOC wants to judge whether current activity is anomalous. What should new data be compared against?
questions.why: A baseline captures normal historical performance, so deviations from it stand out.
questions.whyWrong: Logs, captures and NetFlow are data sources that can feed a baseline, but they are not the reference itself.

questions.question: In the three-tier model, which middle tier connects access devices and forwards their traffic toward the core?
questions.why: The distribution tier sits between access and core, aggregating and forwarding access-layer traffic.
questions.whyWrong: Access connects end devices directly, core is the high-speed backbone, and aggregation is not a tier name in this model.

questions.question: A change in a 120-minute window is stuck at the last step after 90 minutes and the manager starts the rollback plan. What happens next?

choices.text: Return the system to its original state before the change
Return the system to step four, the last working step
Leave the change in place and tell users a workaround
Request more time since the change is nearly done

questions.correctText: Return the system to its original state before the change
questions.why: A rollback restores the last known good state from before the change began.
questions.whyWrong: Stopping mid-way leaves a half-applied change, a workaround avoids the required restore, and extra time was not granted.

questions.question: Changes were made to speed up a slow network but users say it feels no faster. How do you prove improvement?

choices.text: Provide a copy of the approved change request
Present a physical network diagram of the changes
Present a logical network diagram of the changes
Show results of a new performance baseline assessment

questions.correctText: Show results of a new performance baseline assessment
questions.why: Comparing a fresh performance baseline with the pre-change one gives hard evidence of speed changes.
questions.whyWrong: Paperwork and diagrams describe the change but do not measure its effect.

questions.question: What protection redirects an attacker to a separate server that holds no real financial data?
questions.why: A honeypot is a monitored decoy that looks valuable and draws attackers away from real systems.
questions.whyWrong: A screened subnet hosts real exposed services, a content filter blocks unwanted content, and a botnet is an attacker's herd of infected machines.

questions.question: Which IPv6 communication type sends a packet to the nearest interface that shares a common address?
questions.why: Anycast assigns one address to several interfaces and routing delivers the packet to the nearest one.
questions.whyWrong: Unicast is one-to-one, multicast is one-to-many, and broadcast is IPv4-only and reaches everyone.

questions.question: Which band gives maximum throughput while staying compatible with 802.11ac?
questions.why: 802.11ac operates in the 5 GHz band.
questions.whyWrong: 2.4 GHz belongs to b/g/n, 6 GHz is Wi-Fi 6E territory, and 3.7 GHz is not a Wi-Fi band.

questions.question: Which ports do FTP and SFTP use?
questions.why: FTP's control port is 21 and SFTP rides SSH on port 22.
questions.whyWrong: Port 23 is Telnet, and 20/21 are both FTP ports with no SFTP.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes primary and secondary DNS servers set up for high availability?

choices.text: Primary holds the original read-write zone records; secondary holds a read-only copy updated by zone transfers
Primary and secondary each serve a different subset of the namespace independently
Primary is caching-only; secondary handles all dynamic updates
Primary is for internal queries only; secondary is for external queries only

questions.correctText: Primary holds the original read-write zone records; secondary holds a read-only copy updated by zone transfers
questions.why: The primary is the editable source of the zone; secondaries keep read-only copies refreshed by zone transfers.
questions.whyWrong: Secondaries mirror the primary rather than splitting the namespace, the primary is not caching-only, and the split is not internal versus external.

questions.question: A WPA-Enterprise system whose backend supports EAP and TTLS needs stronger authentication. What should be implemented?

choices.text: WPA2 with a complex shared key
MAC address filtering with IP filtering

questions.why: 802.1X with EAP-MSCHAPv2 checks each user's own credentials and works with the EAP-capable backend.
questions.whyWrong: A shared key is one secret for everyone, MAC/IP filtering uses spoofable addresses, and a separate PKI does not tie into the EAP/TTLS backend described.

questions.question: Which connection method lets software applications interact with network devices for configuration and management?
questions.why: An API lets programs send requests and receive data from devices programmatically.
questions.whyWrong: A GUI, SSH session and console are human-driven interfaces, not programmatic ones.

questions.question: Which syslog severity level does a warning condition generate?
questions.why: Severity 4 is warning - a problem may occur if no action is taken.
questions.whyWrong: 0 is emergency, 2 is critical, and 6 is informational.

questions.question: Which use case best fits VXLAN between dispersed data centers?
questions.why: VXLAN stretches Layer 2 networks over Layer 3, which is exactly what connecting distant data centers needs.
questions.whyWrong: Branch, IoT and conferencing traffic do not need Layer 2 stretched between sites.

questions.question: A phone maker wants contactless payments like Apple Pay in its handsets. Which technology should be embedded?
questions.why: NFC works at a few centimeters with two-way communication, which tap-to-pay systems rely on.
questions.whyWrong: RFID is one-way tag reading, Bluetooth reaches about 10 m for data exchange, and Wi-Fi is for network access.

questions.question: Which protocol routes between different autonomous systems while keeping optimal paths?
questions.why: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol built for routing between autonomous systems.
questions.whyWrong: OSPF works inside one autonomous system, ICMP carries diagnostics, and DHCP assigns addresses.

questions.question: Intermittent connectivity and sluggish performance appear where switches were interconnected without proper STP. What is the likely cause?
questions.why: Without STP, redundant links loop and broadcast storms drag the network down.
questions.whyWrong: DHCP failure affects addressing, saturation alone does not create loops, and ARP spoofing is an attack, not a topology fault.

questions.question: Which tool most effectively allows only certain permissions on system resources?
questions.why: An access control list grants or denies specific access to specific resources with fine-grained rules.
questions.whyWrong: A firewall filters more broadly, a VPN secures remote transport, and an IDS/IPS only monitors and reacts.

questions.question: Which device receives a signal on one port and re-transmits the same signal out another to extend distance?
questions.why: A repeater regenerates the same signal so it can travel farther.
questions.whyWrong: An access point joins wireless clients to a wired network, a media converter changes media types, and an IDS watches for threats.

questions.question: Which media access method listens before sending and uses a back-off timer after a collision?
questions.why: CSMA/CD detects collisions, stops, sends a jam signal and retries after a random back-off.
questions.whyWrong: CSMA/CA tries to avoid collisions (wireless), token passing only sends while holding the token, and demand priority polls by priority.

questions.question: Which IPv4 address class fits multicast group communication for video conferencing?
questions.why: Class D is reserved for multicast groups.
questions.whyWrong: Classes A, B and C are unicast ranges sized for large, medium and small networks.

questions.question: A failed RAID controller was replaced with a different brand and the server rebuilt and rejoined to the domain. What will be needed?
questions.why: A different controller cannot read the old array, so the RAID must be rebuilt and data restored from the latest backup.
questions.whyWrong: Diagrams and vendor docs help planning but hold no data, and a directly attached array needs no IP address.

questions.question: To build a subnet for a specific host count and have routing pick the most specific path, which addressing aspect matters most?

choices.text: Modify metric values to define preferred paths
