Adjust administrative distance to control route selection
Configure VLAN IDs to segregate traffic
Define the prefix length for subnets

questions.correctText: Define the prefix length for subnets
questions.why: Prefix length sets the network/host split, which controls both subnet size and route specificity.
questions.whyWrong: Metrics and administrative distance rank routes, and VLAN IDs segment traffic - none size a subnet.

questions.question: Which factor do all routers consider when choosing the best path?

choices.text: Physical distance between source and destination
Prefix length of the destination network address
Bandwidth of the links along the path
Number of hops to the destination

questions.correctText: Prefix length of the destination network address
questions.why: Routers always prefer the longest, most specific prefix match first.
questions.whyWrong: Hop count and bandwidth are protocol-specific metrics, and physical distance is not a routing input.

questions.question: A student cannot join an open AP with hidden SSID DionTraining after typing DIONTRAINING, while classmates connect fine. What is the issue?
questions.why: SSIDs are case-sensitive, so the all-caps entry names a different network.
questions.whyWrong: The network is open, so there is no encryption or passphrase to get wrong, and coverage is fine for everyone else.

questions.question: Users cannot reach websites. Which tool shows whether the fault is on the intranet or with the ISP?
questions.why: tracert shows each hop, revealing where the path stops - inside the network or beyond it.
questions.whyWrong: ping only says reachable or not, nslookup checks DNS, and netstat shows local connections.

questions.question: A WPA2/AES workstation gets a 'network security key mismatch' error when connecting. What causes it?
questions.why: That exact error means the entered passphrase does not match the AP's key.
questions.whyWrong: Both sides already agree on WPA2/AES, weak coverage gives a different symptom, and a wrong SSID would not find the network.

questions.question: An IPv6-only segment should auto-generate addresses from router advertisements with no DHCP server. What should be implemented?

choices.text: Enable SLAAC on the IPv6 router
Configure a DHCPv6 server to assign addresses
Set up manual IPv6 assignment per device

questions.correctText: Enable SLAAC on the IPv6 router
questions.why: SLAAC lets hosts build their own addresses from router advertisements plus their interface ID.
questions.whyWrong: DHCPv6 options still need a server, and manual assignment is the opposite of automatic.

questions.question: Which ports do HTTPS and RDP use?
questions.why: HTTPS is 443 and RDP is 3389.
questions.whyWrong: 445 is SMB, 25 is SMTP, and 161 is SNMP.

questions.question: What is the security concern when many cloud customers share the same physical hardware?
questions.why: Resource pooling shares hardware between tenants, raising isolation and side-channel risks.
questions.whyWrong: Elasticity, metering and on-demand describe scaling and billing, not shared-hardware exposure.

questions.question: A vertical cross-connect between IDF floors has no air ducts nearby and must carry 10GBaseT up to 100 m. Which cable fits?
questions.why: Cat6a carries 10 Gbps to 100 m, and with no air-handling space a riser rating is sufficient.
questions.whyWrong: Cat5e tops out at 1 Gbps, and plenum rating is only required in air spaces.

questions.question: A new fiber link between data centers shows no link light with SFP+ modules at both ends. What is most likely?

choices.text: The fiber patch panel is not properly labeled
IP addressing mismatch at both ends
Mismatch between the transceivers at each end
Fiber cables incompatible with the SFP+ transceivers

questions.correctText: Mismatch between the transceivers at each end
questions.why: Mismatched transceiver types, wavelengths or speeds cannot establish a link.
questions.whyWrong: Labeling does not affect the light, IP settings sit above the physical layer, and the cabling matches the installed modules.

questions.question: Which tool captures live traffic on a segment for detailed analysis of protocols, ports and contents?
questions.why: tcpdump captures packets live so their headers and contents can be examined.
questions.whyWrong: ping tests reachability, traceroute maps paths, and nslookup queries DNS.

questions.question: In a federation model, an employee logs in once to the main site and is then automatically authenticated everywhere else. Which type is that?
questions.why: Single sign-on authenticates once and carries that trust to the other services.
questions.whyWrong: MFA adds extra factors, and TouchID/FaceID are biometric methods, not federation.

questions.question: Which method automatically configures IPv6 host addresses?
questions.why: EUI-64 builds the 64-bit interface ID from the device's MAC address.
questions.whyWrong: APIPA is IPv4-only, EIA-568B is a cabling standard, and EBCDIC is a character encoding.

questions.question: What error is recorded when a switch receives an Ethernet frame larger than 1518 bytes?
questions.why: Oversized frames beyond the 1518-byte standard are counted as giants.
questions.whyWrong: Runts are under 64 bytes, CRC errors are checksum failures, and encapsulation is a framing process, not this error.

questions.question: An office Wi-Fi network with many physical devices needs internet access. Which network type fits best?
questions.why: Infrastructure mode uses a central access point to connect many devices, ideal for an office.
questions.whyWrong: Ad hoc has no central point, a VPN is for secure remote access, and a WAN links distant sites.

questions.question: A wireless client set to AES tries to join an 802.11ac AP set to WEP. Which issue occurs?
questions.why: The client and AP speak different encryption schemes, so they cannot communicate.
questions.whyWrong: A bad passphrase gives a key-mismatch error, and coverage or SSID problems present differently.

questions.question: Which service provides authentication, authorization and accounting through a centralized database, with challenge/response and encrypted passwords?
questions.why: TACACS+ is the AAA protocol with a central database, challenge/response and encrypted password handling.
questions.whyWrong: ISAKMP sets up IPsec keys, MFA is a general factor concept, and NAC checks device compliance.

questions.question: A technician terminates a new copper cable between two legacy switches and no connection forms. What is most likely?

choices.text: Cable has RJ-11 instead of RJ-45 connectors

questions.why: Legacy switches without MDIX need a crossover cable switch-to-switch; straight-through will not link.
questions.whyWrong: Bend radius is a fiber concern, RJ-11 plugs visibly do not fit, and a crossover is exactly what was needed.

questions.question: Which feature remembers the first Layer 2 address seen on a switch port and blocks a swapped-in laptop?
questions.why: Port security with sticky MAC learning binds the port to the first device's address.
questions.whyWrong: An ACL filters higher-layer traffic, NAC checks compliance, and 802.1X asks for credentials rather than remembering an address.

questions.question: A new building has no records of which patch panel port serves which office jack. Which tool builds the wiring map?
questions.why: A tone generator and probe trace a specific pair through bundles and panels to its far end.
questions.whyWrong: A TDR finds faults, a cable tester verifies wiring, and a loopback adapter tests a device port.

questions.question: Two switches have redundant links; one link stays inactive even when moved to another port. Why?
questions.why: STP deliberately blocks the redundant port to keep the topology loop-free.
questions.whyWrong: SSID is a wireless name, mirroring copies traffic for monitoring, and IGRP is a Layer 3 protocol.

questions.question: A resolver with no cached answer asks another server that does the work of finding the definitive answer. What is this called?
questions.why: In a recursive lookup the server chases down the final answer on the client's behalf.
questions.whyWrong: Primary, secondary and authoritative describe server roles, not this query process.

questions.question: For an 802.11h network in dense traffic under strict channel regulation, which aspect should be prioritized?
questions.why: Transmit Power Control lowers power to only what is needed, cutting interference in crowded, regulated airspace.
questions.whyWrong: MIMO adds capacity, beamforming aims signals, and fast roaming speeds AP handoffs - none manage power.

questions.question: What does the 'A' stand for in the CIA triad?
questions.why: The triad is Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.
questions.whyWrong: Accessibility, authentication and acceptance are not triad members.

questions.question: An unstable fiber link shows high CRC errors. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Incompatible transceiver types at each end

questions.correctText: Incompatible transceiver types at each end
questions.why: Mixing single-mode and multimode optics or wavelengths corrupts the signal and drives CRC errors up.
questions.whyWrong: Fiber ignores EMI and needs no shielding, and power allocation concerns PoE devices.

questions.question: Which tool pinpoints the cause of suspected congestion behind slow access to resources?
questions.why: A protocol analyzer shows which traffic consumes bandwidth and when, exposing the congestion source.
questions.whyWrong: A Wi-Fi analyzer only covers wireless, a toner traces cables, and a cable tester checks integrity.

questions.question: Which cloud characteristic lets you add storage and resources as fast as possible?
questions.why: Rapid elasticity scales resources up on demand without buying and installing hardware.
questions.whyWrong: Pooling shares resources, and measured/metered services track usage and billing.

questions.question: Software broadcasts per-department stats to monitoring servers, adding broadcast traffic. How do you minimize it?

choices.text: Add a router and create a separate segment for monitored hosts
Place each department in its own VLAN to increase broadcast domains

questions.correctText: Place each department in its own VLAN to increase broadcast domains
questions.why: Each VLAN is its own broadcast domain, so broadcasts stay inside one department.
questions.whyWrong: More switches or collision domains do not contain broadcasts, and one extra segment does not split the departments.

questions.question: A user's wireless router cannot get DHCP from an office jack, but her laptop can. What is most likely?

choices.text: DHCP requests from access points are blocked
Only allow-listed MAC addresses can connect

questions.correctText: Only allow-listed MAC addresses can connect
questions.why: MAC allow-listing admits only approved addresses; the laptop is listed and the router is not.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not single out the other mechanisms; the pattern - one known device works, an unknown one does not - matches allow-listing.

questions.question: Which disaster recovery site type has little to no hardware and may take days or weeks to become ready?
questions.why: A cold site is mostly space and utilities with little installed equipment.
questions.whyWrong: A warm site is equipped but lacks live data, a hot site mirrors production in real time, and a cloud site is virtual.

questions.question: What is the expected output of nmap -p 22,80,443 10.50.30.2?

choices.text: An error that nmap cannot scan multiple ports at once
A report of all devices using the services with their MAC addresses
Version and revision numbers of the services on those ports
A list showing the status of ports 22, 80 and 443 on that server

questions.correctText: A list showing the status of ports 22, 80 and 443 on that server
questions.why: nmap with -p reports whether each listed port on that host is open, closed or filtered.
questions.whyWrong: nmap scans multiple ports fine, reports on the target host only, and version detection needs -sV.

questions.question: A patch panel port is punched down on only the middle two pins (4 and 5). What was it cabled for?
questions.why: Plain old telephone service needs just one pair for send and receive.
questions.whyWrong: 10BaseT needs two pairs, and 568A/568B use all four pairs.

questions.question: Which metric is the variable delay a client experiences receiving packets from a sender?
questions.why: Jitter is the variation in packet delay, which hurts real-time traffic like VoIP and video.
questions.whyWrong: Latency is the overall delay, throughput is delivered data rate, and bandwidth is theoretical capacity.

questions.question: Traffic meant for a secure VLAN is being reached from an unsecured VLAN. What is most likely?

choices.text: DHCP is assigning secure-VLAN addresses to unsecured devices
The firewall is configured to allow all traffic

questions.why: VLAN hopping crafts traffic that jumps VLAN boundaries, often abusing trunk negotiation on untrusted ports.
questions.whyWrong: DHCP errors misaddress devices without crossing VLANs, and firewall or default settings do not by themselves hop VLANs.

questions.question: A remote-office fiber link shows excessive dB loss after a switch was moved and a new patch cable installed. What is most likely?
questions.why: Contaminated connector ends - even skin oil - cause heavy loss; cleaning them is the fix.
questions.whyWrong: A room move cannot exceed fiber distance, no sharp bend was mentioned, and the plant uses one fiber type.

questions.question: Which technology splits corporate wireless into an administrative network for company devices and an untrusted network for BYOD?
questions.why: VLANs create separate virtual networks on the same physical gear and keep them apart without a router.
questions.whyWrong: A VPN is remote access, WPA2 is encryption, and MAC filtering admits devices without creating segments.

questions.question: A switch port's speed was never specified. What most likely happens?

choices.text: The connected device dictates speed and the port passively adapts
The port defaults to the lowest possible speed
The port disables itself until speed is set manually
The port and device negotiate the highest common speed

questions.correctText: The port and device negotiate the highest common speed
questions.why: Auto-negotiation is the default, settling on the fastest speed both sides support.
questions.whyWrong: Negotiation is mutual, and ports neither shut down nor drop to the minimum by default.

questions.question: A CEO hesitates to move all company data, including sensitive data, to SaaS. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: SaaS will increase exposure to malware and hackers
The SaaS solution is incompatible with the current browser
Moving data will decrease internal network performance
They will lose full control over data and resources

questions.correctText: They will lose full control over data and resources
questions.why: Handing data to a SaaS provider means giving up direct control over it and its protection.
questions.whyWrong: There is no evidence SaaS is inherently more exposed, web-based apps run in any browser, and moving data out usually relieves the internal network.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of subinterfaces?

choices.text: Separate physical interfaces on a device into multiple connections
Interfaces reserved for high-speed data transfer
Interfaces used for connecting different network segments
Virtual interfaces created on a single physical interface, partitioning it into multiple logical interfaces

questions.correctText: Virtual interfaces created on a single physical interface, partitioning it into multiple logical interfaces
questions.why: Subinterfaces are virtual partitions of one physical port, commonly used for VLAN routing.
questions.whyWrong: They are not physical, not speed-specific, and segment connection is a use, not their defining trait.

questions.question: Which statement best describes why 802.1Q tagging matters?

choices.text: To bundle several ports together for bandwidth and redundancy
To ensure voice traffic is prioritized over data traffic
To create a single VLAN spanning multiple switches without tagging
To allow multiple VLANs over one physical link between switches

questions.correctText: To allow multiple VLANs over one physical link between switches
questions.why: 802.1Q tags let one trunk carry many VLANs while keeping their traffic separate.
questions.whyWrong: Bundling ports is link aggregation, voice priority is QoS, and untagged spanning contradicts tagging's purpose.

questions.question: What is the most suitable low-cost way to secure internal communications with better authentication, without third-party CAs?

choices.text: Purchase enterprise SSL certificates from a trusted CA
Employ IPsec tunnels for data encryption

questions.why: Self-signed PKI gives authentication and encryption without paying an external CA.
questions.whyWrong: Buying CA certificates costs money and adds outside reliance, single-factor is weaker, and IPsec encrypts without providing the authentication described.

questions.question: Which of the following is a DNS record type?
questions.why: PTR records map an IP address back to a hostname for reverse lookups.
questions.whyWrong: TTL is a lifetime value, DHCP assigns addresses, and LDAP is a directory protocol.

questions.question: Which term is the maximum amount of data, measured in time, an organization is willing to lose during an outage?
questions.why: The recovery point objective caps how much data loss, in time, is acceptable.
questions.whyWrong: RTO caps restore time, MTTR is average repair time, and MTBF is average time between failures.

questions.question: Which DNS configuration should be enhanced so internal queries resolve with trusted, verified records while external queries use cache?
questions.why: An authoritative server holds the definitive records for its zones, so its answers are trusted.
questions.whyWrong: Caching-only and non-authoritative servers rely on stored answers, and forwarding servers pass queries elsewhere.

questions.question: What should a technician use to troubleshoot half the office being unable to reach a shared printer?
questions.why: A network diagram shows how everything connects, the starting point for tracing a shared-device fault.
questions.whyWrong: Baselines track performance over time, backups restore data, and vendor docs describe a single device.

questions.question: Which port should be blacklisted to protect against ransomware abusing the Windows SMB protocol?
questions.why: SMB uses port 445 (and 139); blocking 445 stops internet-borne SMB attacks like WannaCry.
questions.whyWrong: 123 is NTP, 143 is IMAP, and 514 is syslog.

questions.question: A new Smart TV shows the address 169.254.0.24. Which address type is that?
questions.why: 169.254.x.x is the APIPA range a device self-assigns when DHCP is unreachable.
questions.whyWrong: Private addresses are the RFC1918 ranges, public addresses are internet-routable, and the site treats IPv6-style link-local as a different category.

questions.question: Which parameter must be adjusted to enable jumbo frames on a device?
questions.why: Jumbo frames exceed the standard 1500-byte MTU, so the interface MTU must be raised (up to about 9000).
questions.whyWrong: TTL limits packet lifetime, duplex sets send/receive behavior, and speed is the link rate.

questions.question: What is the network ID for the host 201.58.12.245/28?
questions.why: A /28 block holds 16 addresses, and .245 falls in the block starting at .240.
questions.whyWrong: The other choices start blocks that do not contain .245.

questions.question: A small office wants straightforward Wi-Fi security with no extensive authentication server. Which choice and reason fit?

choices.text: Enterprise, because it is easier to manage for small networks with minimal configuration
Pre-shared key (PSK), because it is simpler and needs no external authentication server
Pre-shared key (PSK), because it is faster due to lack of encryption
Enterprise, because it offers higher security through an external authentication server

questions.correctText: Pre-shared key (PSK), because it is simpler and needs no external authentication server
questions.why: PSK uses one shared passphrase and no authentication server, suiting small simple networks.
questions.whyWrong: Enterprise needs a RADIUS-style server and more setup, and PSK still encrypts - speed is not its advantage.

questions.question: Which communication type sends a direct request from one host to a server?
questions.why: Unicast is strictly one sender to one receiver.
questions.whyWrong: Broadcast reaches everyone, multicast reaches a group, and anycast reaches the nearest of a group.

questions.question: Five lab servers go in a screened subnet carved from 187.15.3.0/24 using the minimum addresses. Which CIDR fits?
questions.why: Five hosts plus network and broadcast need 7 addresses, so the 8-address /29 block is the minimum.
questions.whyWrong: /30 has only 4 addresses, while /28 and /27 allocate more than needed.

questions.question: In a high-availability test a fiber cut did not trigger automatic re-routing. Which routing type is in use?
questions.why: Static routes are entered by hand and never adapt on their own, so traffic stays put until someone changes them.
questions.whyWrong: Distance vector, hybrid and dynamic routing all react to link loss and re-route automatically.

questions.question: Policy says every infrastructure device must send system-level messages to one central server so errors can be reviewed in one place. What should be implemented?
questions.why: A syslog server collects standardized log messages from devices at one central point for monitoring.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not single out the others; SSO and TACACS+ handle authentication and a Wi-Fi analyzer examines wireless, not device logs.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a server rack and a switch rack?

choices.text: Server racks store only servers; switch racks hold a variety including servers, routers and UPS units
Server racks need higher power load and cooling; switch racks house lower-power, lower-heat devices
Switch racks are typically smaller because switches take less space
Server racks have built-in cable management; switch racks do not

questions.correctText: Server racks need higher power load and cooling; switch racks house lower-power, lower-heat devices
questions.why: Servers draw more power and produce more heat, so their racks need more power and cooling planning.
questions.whyWrong: Switch racks are not a mixed-equipment category, rack size follows the room and gear rather than rack type, and both types can have cable management.

questions.question: When is static routing the better choice over dynamic routing?

choices.text: When automatic rerouting based on real-time traffic is required
In a small network where a direct path does not change often
In a large network with complex algorithms and multiple protocols
In a rapidly changing network needing frequent route adjustments

questions.correctText: In a small network where a direct path does not change often
questions.why: Manual routes suit small, stable networks whose paths rarely change.
questions.whyWrong: Automatic rerouting, large complex networks and fast-changing topologies are exactly where dynamic routing wins.

questions.question: Which weakness exists in WPS-enabled wireless networks?
questions.why: WPS checks each half of its PIN separately, shrinking the search to roughly 11,000 tries.
questions.whyWrong: The short IV and 40-bit key are WEP flaws, and TKIP was WPA's improvement over WEP.

questions.question: Workstations must hide their internal IP addresses when requesting resources across a WAN. What best meets that policy?
questions.why: NAT rewrites internal addresses to a public address as packets leave for the WAN.
questions.whyWrong: A DMZ exposes services, a VPN extends a private network, and OSPF is a routing protocol - none hide source addresses.

questions.question: Data centers route Asia/Europe/Africa traffic through Istanbul and the Americas through Mexico City. Which topology is that?
questions.why: Each regional center acts as a hub and the surrounding sites are spokes that route through it.
questions.whyWrong: A bus shares one medium, a ring passes traffic in a loop, and spine-and-leaf is a within-data-center fabric.

questions.question: Which wireless technology uses MIMO on non-overlapping channels to increase bandwidth?
questions.why: 802.11n brought MIMO to Wi-Fi for higher throughput.
questions.whyWrong: The a, b and g standards predate MIMO support.

questions.question: Which Ethernet standard is used with single-mode fiber?
questions.why: 10GBase-LR is the 10-gigabit standard built for single-mode fiber.
questions.whyWrong: SR targets multimode fiber, and the -T standards run on copper.

questions.question: A power plant has business and ICS/SCADA networks. What should be implemented FIRST to improve SCADA defenses?
questions.why: SCADA systems use a narrow set of known commands, so a strict IPS can block anything unusual.
questions.whyWrong: Logs only record events, untested patches can break control systems, and such systems often run non-standard OSes that antivirus cannot cover.

questions.question: Fiber video is being added to a LAN using one connector for transmit and a separate one for receive. Which connector type is that?
questions.why: ST connectors are single-strand fiber connectors commonly used in LAN fiber links.
questions.whyWrong: MTRJ combines transmit and receive in one connector, and RJ-45/RJ-11 are copper connectors.

questions.question: Two switches linked by multiple Ethernet cables carry several critical servers. How do you gain bandwidth and redundancy?

choices.text: Enable link aggregation using LACP on the connecting ports
Configure the native VLAN to include all server traffic
Assign a dedicated VLAN for each server connection
Set up a voice VLAN to prioritize server traffic

questions.correctText: Enable link aggregation using LACP on the connecting ports
questions.why: LACP bundles the links into one logical link, adding capacity and a fallback if one fails.
questions.whyWrong: VLAN changes segregate or prioritize traffic but add neither bandwidth nor link redundancy.

questions.question: Two buildings are being connected with fiber for high speed. Which option is best for long distance?
questions.why: Single-mode's single light path loses less signal, so it reaches much farther.
questions.whyWrong: Multimode disperses over distance, DAC is for short in-rack runs, and coax cannot match fiber speed at range.

questions.question: Which DNS record type stores DKIM and SPF information?
questions.why: TXT records carry the text-based data used by SPF, DKIM and DMARC email authentication.
questions.whyWrong: SOA names zone authority, PTR does reverse lookups, and SRV locates services.

questions.question: A firewalled network has internal, DMZ and external zones; internal hosts need outbound internet but must not be directly reachable from it. Which addressing solution fits?
questions.why: Private addresses keep hosts behind NAT, reachable out but not directly in.
questions.whyWrong: APIPA is a DHCP fallback, classless describes subnetting style, and Teredo is an IPv6 transition tunnel.

questions.question: A 2.4 GHz AP is installed where neighbors run B/G/N networks. Which channel set maximizes spacing?
questions.why: Channels 1, 6 and 11 are the non-overlapping set in the 2.4 GHz band.
questions.whyWrong: The other sets overlap each other; the site notes only 1/6/11 avoid overlap.

questions.question: What capability should you expect from deploying a SIEM system?

choices.text: Automatic resolution and patching of all indicated vulnerabilities
Real-time analysis of security alerts from network hardware and applications
Acting as a physical barrier to unauthorized access

questions.correctText: Real-time analysis of security alerts from network hardware and applications
questions.why: A SIEM analyzes security alerts in real time so threats can be spotted and answered quickly.
questions.whyWrong: It does not auto-patch, speed up transfers, or physically block anyone.

questions.question: In infrastructure as code, which aspect means storing configuration files in a shared location all team members can reach?
questions.why: A central repository (like Git) stores the files with version control for the whole team.
questions.whyWrong: CI automates integration and testing, configuration management maintains desired states, and templates are prebuilt starting points.

questions.question: Which statement best describes how a DHCP reservation works?

choices.text: Leasing a set of reserved addresses by category
Assigning options to computers by priority
Matching a MAC address to an IP address within the DHCP scope
Letting switches assign IPs from a reserved pool

questions.correctText: Matching a MAC address to an IP address within the DHCP scope
questions.why: The server pins one IP in the scope to a client's MAC, so that client always receives it.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not break down the other options; reservations are a server-side MAC-to-IP match, not a switch or category function.

questions.question: After a breach, a capture device is attached to the server switch facing the screened subnet. What makes it receive all server traffic?
questions.why: Port mirroring copies traffic from the monitored ports to the port feeding the capture device.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not detail the others; 802.1X authenticates, 802.1Q tags VLANs, and port security limits MACs - none copy traffic.

questions.question: In VXLAN, what is the purpose of the VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI)?

choices.text: Differentiate between different VXLAN overlay networks
Uniquely identify each VXLAN tunnel endpoint
Designate source and destination IPs for VXLAN traffic

questions.correctText: Differentiate between different VXLAN overlay networks
questions.why: Each overlay segment gets its own 24-bit VNI so endpoints keep overlays separate.
questions.whyWrong: The site states the other descriptions are not what the VNI does, without detailing each.

questions.question: A new 802.11ac AP replaces an old AP with the same SSID, encryption and password; most devices connect but a very old printer will not. What is most likely?

choices.text: Frequency mismatch between AP and printer
Incorrect channel configured on the AP

questions.correctText: Frequency mismatch between AP and printer
questions.why: The printer is 2.4 GHz-only while the ac AP serves 5 GHz, so they can never hear each other.
questions.whyWrong: Other devices connect fine, ruling out power and password, and ac channels are set automatically.

questions.question: A tape storage facility is told not to recycle old backup tapes until a forensic investigation ends. What is the most likely reason?
questions.why: A legal hold requires preserving relevant material until the hold is lifted.
questions.whyWrong: Discovery is the evidence-exchange phase, chain of custody is the handling log, and a transport request moves data.

questions.question: What defines how much bandwidth various protocols may use on the network?
questions.why: Traffic shaping prioritizes and delays traffic classes to manage bandwidth use.
questions.whyWrong: HA removes single points of failure, fault tolerance survives component failure, and load balancing spreads work across resources.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Port Address Translation (PAT)?

choices.text: A method of encrypting packets for secure transmission over a public network
A type of NAT where multiple private IPs map to a single public IP using different port numbers
A technique to prioritize traffic based on predefined rules
A protocol for dynamically assigning IP addresses

questions.correctText: A type of NAT where multiple private IPs map to a single public IP using different port numbers
questions.why: PAT lets many private hosts share one public address, distinguished by port numbers.
questions.whyWrong: Encryption describes SSL/IPsec, prioritizing describes QoS, and dynamic assignment describes DHCP.

questions.question: What must be added to a VLAN's gateway to actually improve the VLAN's security?
questions.why: An ACL on the gateway filters the routed traffic between VLANs; a VLAN alone adds no real control.
questions.whyWrong: STP prevents loops, and split horizon and hold-down timers are routing-loop safeguards.

questions.question: Which technology gives IP packets source authentication, integrity via hashing, and confidentiality via encryption?
questions.why: IPsec combines authentication, integrity checking and encryption for IP traffic.
questions.whyWrong: The site notes the others each offer only part of that set, without detailing each one.

questions.question: Heavy snow blocks travel during multiple outages. From home, what should be used to reach the datacenter and troubleshoot?
questions.why: SSH (or a VPN) gives an encrypted tunnel for remote work.
questions.whyWrong: SNMP only monitors, and Telnet and HTTP send data in the clear.

questions.question: A cable pulled past a sharp edge has exposed conductors now touching each other. What condition results?
questions.why: Touching conductors create a short circuit, which a cable tester reports as a short.
questions.whyWrong: An open is the opposite (no connection), ESD is a static discharge, and crosstalk is signal coupling between pairs.

questions.question: In STP, how is the root bridge ID determined?

choices.text: The switch's lowest MAC address combined with its port number
The bridge priority combined with the switch's MAC address
The switch model number followed by its serial number
The switch's IP address combined with its subnet mask

questions.correctText: The bridge priority combined with the switch's MAC address
questions.why: The bridge ID pairs the configurable priority with the MAC address; the lowest combined value wins.
questions.whyWrong: Port numbers, model/serial numbers and IP details play no part in the bridge ID.

questions.question: After a DMZ security device was replaced, external users can no longer reach an application remotely. Which device was most likely misconfigured?
questions.why: The firewall guards the DMZ and denies by default unless its rules allow the application traffic.
questions.whyWrong: A content filter judges content, DHCP assigns addresses, and DNS resolves names - none gate remote access.

questions.question: A relative 100 miles away has a problem on a Windows 10 laptop. Which technology gives the easiest graphical remote access?
questions.why: RDP shows the Windows desktop so you can work on it as if you were there.
questions.whyWrong: Telnet and SSH are text-only, and a VPN alone only connects networks without controlling the machine.

questions.question: A research station in dense forest needs internet where wired options are impossible. Which technology is most reliable?
questions.why: Satellite service reaches remote areas regardless of terrain and tree cover.
questions.whyWrong: HF radio degrades in forest, microwave needs clear line of sight, and cellular coverage is unlikely there.

questions.question: An admin implemented firewalls, patching and security policies by best practice. What verifies the controls are really in place?
questions.why: Penetration testing probes the systems for exploitable weaknesses, confirming the controls work.
questions.whyWrong: AAA testing alone is too narrow, DR testing checks recovery plans, and SPOF testing checks resilience points.

questions.question: Which port must be open for NTP time synchronization?
questions.why: NTP synchronizes clocks over port 123.
questions.whyWrong: 143 is IMAP, 3389 is RDP, and 389 is LDAP.

questions.question: A solution was just implemented for a network issue. What is the next troubleshooting step?

choices.text: Document the solution and move on
Escalate the solution to management for approval
Take a break before verifying effectiveness
Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures if applicable

questions.correctText: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures if applicable
questions.why: First confirm the whole system works again, then add preventive measures; documentation follows.
questions.whyWrong: Documenting or escalating before verifying skips the proof that the fix worked.

questions.question: Two campus buildings 200 meters apart will be linked directly by wire. Which cable type is most appropriate?
questions.why: Single-mode fiber covers that distance without meaningful loss and ignores EMI.
questions.whyWrong: Copper options are length-limited and EMI-prone, and coax lacks fiber's bandwidth at that range.

questions.question: Which technique monitors network traffic without disrupting normal operations?
questions.why: Mirroring sends a copy of traffic to an analyzer while the original flows untouched.
questions.whyWrong: STP prevents loops, NAT translates addresses, and tagging marks VLANs.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly associated with port 53?
questions.why: DNS answers name-resolution queries on port 53.
questions.whyWrong: FTP uses 20/21, HTTP 80, and SSH 22.

questions.question: A multi-story house has slow Wi-Fi far from the router. Which router feature improves performance across floors and distances?
questions.why: Band steering moves each device to the band that suits its location and conditions.
questions.whyWrong: A single band alone is a trade-off - 2.4 reaches farther, 5 and 6 are faster but shorter-range and less compatible.

questions.question: A company runs a 5 GHz security system. Which standard can NOT be used to provide a 2.4 GHz network?
questions.why: 802.11ac is 5 GHz-only, so it cannot offer 2.4 GHz service.
questions.whyWrong: b and g are 2.4 GHz standards, and n can run on 2.4 GHz.

questions.question: Devices in certain office areas keep losing connection while the network overall works. What is most probable?
questions.why: Dead or weak zones mean those areas simply lack adequate coverage.
questions.whyWrong: Roaming affects moving clients, disassociation is a client behavior, and degradation describes weakening signal rather than missing coverage areas.

questions.question: A media converter must join new single-mode fiber to existing Cat 6a. Which converter type is needed?
questions.why: The converter changes the fiber link into ethernet over the Cat 6a plant.
questions.whyWrong: Every other option involves coax, which is not part of this link.

questions.question: Which of these would NOT help defend against a zero-day threat?
questions.why: By definition no patch exists yet for a zero-day, so patching cannot stop it.
questions.whyWrong: Segmentation, whitelisting and threat intelligence can still limit or warn about the attack.

questions.question: Choosing a rack for a server, switch and patch panel with room to grow - which issue is critical?

choices.text: Proximity of the rack to the main power supply

questions.why: The rack must safely carry the current gear plus future additions.
questions.whyWrong: Looks do not matter functionally, and power proximity and cable management are secondary conveniences.

questions.question: Performance suddenly drops across several departments with no known changes. What is the first step?

choices.text: Immediately contact the ISP to increase bandwidth
Determine if anything has changed in the configuration or environment
Upgrade all network hardware to the latest models
Reboot all servers and networking devices without further investigation

questions.correctText: Determine if anything has changed in the configuration or environment
questions.why: Checking for recent changes is the starting point of methodical troubleshooting.
questions.whyWrong: Upgrades, reboots and bandwidth purchases without a diagnosis are costly guesses.

questions.question: A LAN media server pings fine and firewalls are off, yet it will not stream to subscribed workstations. Which technology most likely needs reconfiguring?
questions.why: Streaming to subscribers uses multicast, which must be configured to reach the group members.
questions.whyWrong: Unicast is one-to-one, broadcast floods everyone (IPv4 only), and anycast targets the nearest receiver.

questions.question: In IaC, which aspect ensures changes by different team members do not conflict?
questions.why: Version-control conflict identification flags and helps resolve overlapping edits.
questions.whyWrong: Testing validates configs, CI automates integration, and provisioning creates resources - none resolve edit conflicts.

questions.question: What does the First Hop Redundancy Protocol (FHRP) do?

choices.text: Routes packets between subnets and devices on a LAN
Provides redundancy for the default gateway in a LAN
Balances loads across multiple servers in a server farm

questions.correctText: Provides redundancy for the default gateway in a LAN
questions.why: FHRP keeps a backup gateway ready so hosts keep connectivity if the main one fails.
questions.whyWrong: It does not route between subnets, balance server loads, or secure traffic.

questions.question: A coworker installed a free game found online; since then the computer is strange and extremely slow. What were they most likely a victim of?
questions.why: Malicious software from an untrusted download explains the odd, slow behavior.
questions.whyWrong: Nothing mentions locked files (ransomware), a deceptive message (phishing), or password guessing (brute-force).

questions.question: After a new subnetting scheme, some employees cannot reach shared folders or printers despite having connectivity. What is the likely cause?
questions.why: A wrong mask makes devices treat local resources as remote (or vice versa), breaking access.
questions.whyWrong: Old switches affect performance, DNS faults affect names, and Wi-Fi interference affects wireless links - none are subnetting faults.

questions.question: A design has internet, DMZ, internal and administrative segments. From which segment should routers and switches accept SSH?
questions.why: Management access is restricted to the trusted administrative network, used as a jump point.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail each alternative; internet is untrusted, the DMZ is semi-trusted, and the general internal LAN is too broad.

questions.question: What is the BEST reason to decommission outdated network devices and systems?

choices.text: Reduce redundancy and return the device for an environmental credit
Streamline network management and decrease operational costs
Remove potential security risks and optimize network performance
Improve efficiency because new devices use fewer network resources

questions.correctText: Remove potential security risks and optimize network performance
questions.why: Unsupported old gear carries unpatched risks and drags performance; removing it protects the network.
questions.whyWrong: Cost and management savings are side benefits, and recycling credits are not the main driver.

questions.question: A DNS server is not resolving one hostname. Which command queries DNS and gives diagnostic detail?
questions.why: nslookup queries DNS servers directly and reports how resolution succeeds or fails.
questions.whyWrong: ping hides DNS detail, tcpdump captures packets, and traceroute maps paths.

questions.question: Before an upgrade, a specific tested, approved configuration must be applied to new devices for consistency and low risk. Which configuration is that?
questions.why: The production configuration is the approved live-environment standard for the upgrade.
questions.whyWrong: A backup is for recovery, a golden config is for initial setup or resets, and prototype is not a production standard.

questions.question: Which syslog severity level means the system has become unstable?
questions.why: Level 0 is emergency, the most severe on the 0-to-7 scale.
questions.whyWrong: 1 is alert, 5 is notice, and 7 is debugging.

questions.question: Which measure ensures only authorized devices connect to a port by requiring authentication first?
questions.why: 802.1X authenticates a device (often via RADIUS) before the port grants access.
questions.whyWrong: MAC filtering and port security check addresses without authentication, and ACLs filter traffic rather than authenticate ports.

questions.question: HQ must remotely configure branch routers securely. What is the MOST secure approach that still allows remote access?

choices.text: Configure remote router ACLs to permit only HTTP traffic
Configure remote router ACLs to permit only Telnet traffic

questions.why: A separate out-of-band management network keeps administration off the production path and secured.
questions.whyWrong: HTTP and Telnet are unencrypted, and a dial-up modem invites war-dialing and is slow.

questions.question: Which client-to-site VPN lets users reach corporate resources with no dedicated client software installed?
questions.why: A clientless VPN runs in the browser over SSL, so nothing needs installing.
questions.whyWrong: SSL VPN is the broader family, and IPsec/PPTP setups normally need client software.

questions.question: Why advocate conducting validation tests?

choices.text: Comprehensive audit of compliance with international data protection regulations
Assess physical security of data centers and backup sites
Realistic simulation of disaster scenarios to confirm DR and BCP effectiveness
Hands-on technical training for IT staff on new software/hardware

questions.correctText: Realistic simulation of disaster scenarios to confirm DR and BCP effectiveness
questions.why: Validation tests simulate disasters to prove the recovery and continuity plans actually work.
questions.whyWrong: Audits check compliance, training builds skills, and physical assessments check sites - none rehearse the plans.

questions.question: What is the expected output of an Nmap scan using the -sT flag?

choices.text: Operating system details of the target
A list of open TCP ports on the target
A comprehensive list of all devices on the network
Versions of services running on the target

questions.correctText: A list of open TCP ports on the target
questions.why: -sT is a TCP connect scan, so it reports which TCP ports are open.
questions.whyWrong: Device listing is a different scan, service versions need -sV, and OS detection needs -O.

questions.question: Which protocol establishes a secure, encrypted VPN tunnel that can start from a web browser?
questions.why: An SSL VPN launches from a standard browser (today usually its successor, TLS).
questions.whyWrong: IPsec VPNs are not browser-initiated, PPTP is obsolete, and PPP just links two systems.

questions.question: A new branch router is configured; local connectivity works and internet service is active, yet devices cannot reach the internet. What is most likely missing?
questions.why: Without a default route, packets with no specific route have nowhere to go.
questions.whyWrong: DHCP relay serves address requests, NAT is secondary to having a route, and the SSID is a Wi-Fi setting.

questions.question: Which practice reduces the attack surface by removing unnecessary features and tightening a device's settings?
questions.why: Hardening strips unneeded functions and locks down configuration to cut exposure.
questions.whyWrong: Patching fixes known flaws, encryption protects data, and VLANs segment traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is a connection-oriented protocol?
questions.why: TCP sets up a connection, confirms delivery and retransmits losses for reliability.
questions.whyWrong: UDP, ICMP and NetBIOS send without a prior connection or delivery guarantee.

questions.question: Which pair of authentication factors qualifies as true 2FA?
questions.why: A smartcard (something you have) plus a PIN (something you know) mixes two factor types.
questions.whyWrong: Pairs from one category count as a single factor; the site spells out the username/password case and treats the other same-type pairs the same way.

questions.question: A remote office performs poorly; you must compare traffic patterns against performance baselines. Which tool should you use?
questions.why: A NetFlow analyzer reveals traffic flows, patterns and the applications behind them.
questions.whyWrong: An IP scanner inventories devices, a spectrum analyzer measures RF, and a terminal emulator only provides access.

questions.question: Which DNS server type is the original source for a domain's records, with direct control over updates?
questions.why: The primary holds the master copy and is the authoritative source for changes.
questions.whyWrong: A secondary copies the primary, caching-only stores past answers, and recursive servers query others without holding records.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should be purchased and configured so communications stay secure wherever she connects?

choices.text: International data roaming plan on her cellphone
Local SIM card for her smartphone

questions.why: A VPN encrypts traffic over any network she joins, including public Wi-Fi.
questions.whyWrong: The phone-focused options change how she connects but do not secure the traffic by themselves.

questions.question: New switches go into an IDF with no backup power. Which combination best ensures power continuity and distribution?
questions.why: The UPS covers outages while the PDU distributes power to the switches.
questions.whyWrong: Surge protection and regulation guard quality but provide neither backup (first and third) nor distribution (fourth).

questions.question: You must check whether DHCP snooping is enabled on a network device. Which CLI command do you use?
questions.why: show config displays the running configuration, where the snooping setting appears.
questions.whyWrong: show interface gives interface stats, show route gives the routing table, and show diagnostic gives hardware/software detail.

questions.question: (Select all that apply) Which discovery protocols let devices advertise their identity, capabilities and neighbors?
questions.why: CDP (Cisco's) and LLDP (the open standard) both advertise identity, capabilities and neighbors.
questions.whyWrong: OSPF routes, FTP transfers files, VLANs segment, and SNMP manages and monitors rather than discovers.

questions.question: After an edge switch swap, one user has no network and their NIC shows no LEDs while others are fine. What should you verify NEXT?

choices.text: Verify the device is using the correct cable type
Verify the network interface card is operating properly
Verify the network cable is attached to the new switch
Verify the switch is connected to the router

questions.correctText: Verify the network cable is attached to the new switch
questions.why: The setup worked before the swap, so check what changed first - a patch lead not reseated in the new switch fits the dark LEDs.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the other options; it stresses checking the changed, physical layer first.

questions.question: Which technology is NOT commonly used by a captive portal to redirect users?
questions.why: Portals redirect via HTTP, ICMP or DNS - not DHCP.
questions.whyWrong: The site lists those three common methods and does not discuss DHCP beyond its absence.

questions.question: Installing Cat 6a in an old building: which environmental condition decides between plenum and PVC cabling?
questions.why: If the ceiling space carries air ducts, plenum-rated cable is required because burning PVC releases toxic gas.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not single out the other factors; only the air-handling space drives the rating choice.

questions.question: Which CIDR notation fits 23 devices with the least unused addresses?
questions.why: 23 hosts plus network and broadcast need 25 addresses, so the 32-address /27 is the smallest fit.
questions.whyWrong: /26 wastes addresses with 64, while /28 (16) and /29 (8) are too small.

questions.question: A CSO finds the wireless network reachable from the parking lot. Which setting should change so the signal stays inside while users keep coverage?
questions.why: Lowering transmit power directly shrinks how far the signal travels.
questions.whyWrong: Channel changes fight interference, frequency changes are a blunt tool that hurts indoor coverage, and encryption protects data, not range.

questions.question: Which tool creates a performance baseline by measuring throughput between two new switches?
questions.why: iPerf generates TCP/UDP streams between the switches and measures their throughput.
questions.whyWrong: Traceroute maps hops, an analyzer inspects traffic, and a speed test measures toward an internet server.

questions.question: What does the output of a show config command include?

choices.text: A list of all users currently logged into the switch and their privileges
Dynamic routing protocols in use and their configurations
The complete configuration of the switch, including interfaces and VLANs
Real-time statistics of packet transfers, including errors and throughput

questions.correctText: The complete configuration of the switch, including interfaces and VLANs
questions.why: show config prints the full device configuration - interfaces, VLANs and the rest.
questions.whyWrong: Packet statistics come from show interface, routing config is only one slice, and logged-in users come from session commands.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects IPv4/IPv6 compatibility requirements?

choices.text: IPv4 and IPv6 are inherently incompatible and require separate physical infrastructures
Dual-stack implementation enables coexistence, with devices supporting both simultaneously
IPv6-only networks can seamlessly communicate with IPv4-only networks without additional configuration
NAT is the sole method for interoperability

questions.correctText: Dual-stack implementation enables coexistence, with devices supporting both simultaneously
questions.why: Dual-stack lets devices run both protocols on the same infrastructure during transition.
questions.whyWrong: Separate infrastructures are not required, cross-only communication needs a transition mechanism, and NAT is just one method.

questions.question: Guest Wi-Fi users must see legal and access information before going online. Which technology should be implemented?

choices.text: Configure a VLAN to isolate guest traffic
Deploy additional WPA2-Enterprise authentication for guests
Implement QoS to prioritize guest traffic
Use a captive portal to present the information before internet access is granted

questions.correctText: Use a captive portal to present the information before internet access is granted
questions.why: A captive portal presents the terms page and requires action before access opens.
questions.whyWrong: Enterprise auth secures login, a VLAN isolates, and QoS prioritizes - none present information or collect agreement.

questions.question: ipconfig shows 192.168.1.24, but a web search for 'my IP' returns 35.25.52.11. Why are there two addresses?

choices.text: The way routers handle IP addresses
How a switch handles IP addresses
The way traffic is routed over the internet
The gateway is conducting NAT or PAT

questions.correctText: The gateway is conducting NAT or PAT
questions.why: The PC uses a private address inside, while the gateway's NAT/PAT presents the shared public address outside.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the vaguer alternatives; NAT/PAT at the gateway is the named cause.

questions.question: A switch-router SFP link uses a long cable coiled tightly with a zip tie; logs show weak SFP transmit strength. What is the best explanation?

choices.text: An MMF cable was used instead of an SMF cable
An MTRJ connector was used instead of an ST connector
The SFP module has gone bad and should be replaced
The bend radius of the cable has been exceeded

questions.correctText: The bend radius of the cable has been exceeded
questions.why: Tight coiling bends the fiber past its radius, cracking glass and weakening the transmitted signal.
questions.whyWrong: A bad module would not weaken only transmit, a wrong connector would not fit, and MMF-for-SMF would kill the link entirely.

questions.question: Which command shows the active configuration on a Cisco device?
questions.why: show running-config displays the configuration currently in effect.
questions.whyWrong: startup-config is the saved boot copy, description labels an interface, and show system is not the config command.

questions.question: Which cloud model lets multiple organizations share the costs and benefits of the environment?
questions.why: A community cloud is shared by organizations with common concerns that split the platform and costs.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the other models for this item; private serves one organization and public serves anyone.

questions.question: Which SDN layer lets administrators oversee operations, monitor traffic conditions and display network status?
questions.why: The management plane is where admins observe status and oversee the network.
questions.whyWrong: The application layer requests services, the control layer makes forwarding decisions, and the infrastructure layer moves the data.

questions.question: A company in a heavily industrialized area suffers EMI. Which cable type is an affordable mitigation?
questions.why: Shielded twisted pair's shielding cuts EMI at a modest cost.
questions.whyWrong: Fiber is immune but costlier than needed for short runs per the site, and UTP has no shielding.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 802.1X?

choices.text: A framework for authenticating and authorizing devices before allowing network access
Separate broadcast domains for more efficient transfer speeds
Enable standardized encryption of data on wireless networks
Filter traffic by IP addresses/protocol types and ensure port security

questions.correctText: A framework for authenticating and authorizing devices before allowing network access
questions.why: 802.1X is port-based network access control: authenticate first, then grant access.
questions.whyWrong: Broadcast separation is VLANs' work, and filtering or encryption are not its primary purpose.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of lockable enclosures in network installations?

choices.text: Ensure hardware remains physically secure from unauthorized access
Allow easier maintenance and troubleshooting by organizing cables and devices

questions.correctText: Ensure hardware remains physically secure from unauthorized access
questions.why: Locks keep sensitive equipment safe from tampering, theft and accidental damage.
questions.whyWrong: EMC is about interference, latency comes from design, and organization aids maintenance but is not the lock's purpose.

questions.question: Which component is the primary termination point for cabling from external access providers?
questions.why: The main distribution frame is where providers' outside cables terminate centrally.
questions.whyWrong: An IDF serves a local area, patch panels terminate internal cabling, and routers forward traffic.

questions.question: Which policy describes how a new user requests an account on the enterprise network?
questions.why: An onboarding policy covers everything a new employee needs to start, including getting an account and tools.
questions.whyWrong: BYOD covers personal devices, remote access covers connecting from outside, and the password policy only sets password rules.

questions.question: Which port is insecure and should be blocked right away?
questions.why: Port 23 is Telnet, which sends everything in plaintext.
questions.whyWrong: 22 is SSH, 443 is HTTPS and 995 is secure POP3 - all encrypted.

questions.question: Traffic to one server is extremely high. What should you use to judge whether it is a concern?
questions.why: Comparing current traffic with the baseline shows whether it is actually abnormal.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not single out the other tools for this check.

questions.question: When several routes to one destination exist, which parameter picks the best route based on trustworthiness of the source?
questions.why: Administrative distance rates how trusted a route source is (lower wins).
questions.whyWrong: TTL caps hops, MTU is maximum packet size, and OSPF is a protocol that uses cost.

questions.question: What is the best wireless choice for an office needing up to 54 Mbps on 2.4 GHz?
questions.why: 802.11g delivers 54 Mbps in the 2.4 GHz band and stays compatible with b.
questions.whyWrong: b tops out at 11 Mbps, a is 5 GHz, and ac does not use 2.4 GHz.

questions.question: Which device efficiently distributes power to racks of equipment?
questions.why: A PDU fans power out to many rack devices and uses available amperage efficiently.
questions.whyWrong: A UPS gives emergency power, a generator makes power, and HVAC controls temperature and humidity.

questions.question: Traffic from an external IP reaches an internal host on port 443. Which protocol is expected?
questions.why: Port 443 is HTTPS, whose encryption is provided by TLS.
questions.whyWrong: SSH uses 22, HTTP uses 80 unencrypted, and TFTP uses 69.

questions.question: At which OSI layer is data encapsulated into packets?
questions.why: Layer 3 turns segments into packets.
questions.whyWrong: Layer 4 makes segments, Layer 2 makes frames, and the upper layers handle data rather than packets.

questions.question: You want NMS communication with devices that provides encryption and authentication for management. What is best?
questions.why: SNMPv3 adds authentication and encryption to device management.
questions.whyWrong: Capture and flow analysis only observe traffic, and community strings are basic and unencrypted.

questions.question: A switch interface receives a marked increase in frames of about 4600 bytes. What is causing the issues?
questions.why: Frames far above the 1518-byte maximum are giants.
questions.whyWrong: Runts are undersized, CRC errors are checksum failures, and drops happen when buffers overflow.

questions.question: When troubleshooting DNS, which dig option retrieves all records for a domain?
questions.why: The any type asks for every available record for the domain.
questions.whyWrong: mx, soa and ns each fetch only that single record type.

questions.question: After a new subnet was added, its devices cannot reach the internet while the rest of the network is fine. What is most likely?

choices.text: Default route is missing or misconfigured

questions.correctText: Default route is missing or misconfigured
questions.why: Without a default route, traffic for unknown destinations from the new subnet has no way out.
questions.whyWrong: DHCP and duplicate-address faults affect addressing, and an ACL is less likely than the routing change that came with the subnet.

questions.question: Which environmental factor is most essential for preventing static electricity buildup?
questions.why: Proper humidity keeps static charge from building up and damaging equipment.
questions.whyWrong: Temperature and airflow manage heat, and dust harms gear in other ways - none control static like humidity.

questions.question: Users suffer poor performance while an attacker floods the network with ping requests. What prevents this in future?

choices.text: Modify the ACL to block ICMP traffic

questions.correctText: Modify the ACL to block ICMP traffic
questions.why: Blocking ICMP at the ACL stops the ping flood at the edge.
questions.whyWrong: The flood is a traffic type, not an account or malware problem, and firmware does not filter it.

questions.question: Which activity does NOT belong to the 'identify the problem' step of the methodology?
questions.why: Questioning the obvious belongs to forming a theory of probable cause, the next step.
questions.whyWrong: Gathering information, checking for changes and duplicating the problem are all part of identifying it.

questions.question: Which term describes documenting everyone who has had physical access to or possession of evidence?
questions.why: Chain of custody logs every handover so evidence stays verifiable.
questions.whyWrong: SCP moves files, a legal hold orders preservation, and financial responsibility concerns costs.

questions.question: On a plane, after picking the inflight SSID the browser shows a 404 error. What is the most likely source?
questions.why: The portal page that should appear before access failed to load.
questions.whyWrong: The SSID was chosen from the list, no password was entered, and a plane cabin is small enough for coverage.

questions.question: Which topology gives redundancy with at least two cables and uses a token system to prevent congestion?
questions.why: A dual (FDDI) ring survives one cable failure and its token controls who transmits.
questions.whyWrong: Mesh is redundant but costly with no token, star centers on one node, and bus is a single backbone.

questions.question: A first public web app is hosted privately and needs worldwide access without a public IP per server or exposing server addresses. What should be implemented?

choices.text: Deploy PAT so multiple servers share one public IP using different ports
Use NAT to translate public addresses to private ones for incoming traffic
Assign a public IP address to each server
Implement a VPN between users and the private network

questions.correctText: Deploy PAT so multiple servers share one public IP using different ports
questions.why: PAT lets the servers share one public address, separated by ports, hiding their real addresses.
questions.whyWrong: Per-server public IPs waste addresses and expose servers, plain NAT does not separate servers by port, and a VPN is for private user access, not public publishing.

questions.question: CRC errors climb on a printer's switch port over a 90 m cable and track with high traffic. What is most likely?

choices.text: The cable is too long, beyond maximum distance
A duplex mismatch between switch port and printer
The switch port is on the wrong VLAN
The cable category is lower than the network speed requires

questions.correctText: A duplex mismatch between switch port and printer
questions.why: Mismatched duplex settings produce CRC errors, especially under load.
questions.whyWrong: 90 m is within Ethernet limits, a wrong VLAN blocks access rather than corrupting frames, and cable category affects speed more than checksums.

questions.question: Only finance devices should reach the accounting server. What should be implemented?

choices.text: Increase encryption on the finance wireless network
Implement rules specifying which devices may access the accounting server
Set up a VPN for the finance department
Install a new firewall just for the finance segment

questions.correctText: Implement rules specifying which devices may access the accounting server
questions.why: Access rules (ACLs) allow or deny traffic to the server based on the source devices.
questions.whyWrong: Encryption protects data in transit, a VPN secures connections, and a segment firewall alone does not grant per-device access to one server.

questions.question: What must combine with a threat to create risk?
questions.why: Risk arises when a threat meets a weakness it can exploit.
questions.whyWrong: Exploits and malicious actors are kinds of threat, and mitigation reduces risk rather than creating it.

questions.question: A data center backbone upgrade adds many fiber connections that must stay organized, scalable and easy to troubleshoot. What should be implemented?

choices.text: Deploy a fiber distribution panel to organize and manage the fiber cables
Increase the number of switches to improve segmentation
Add more wireless access points for the higher data rates
Install additional routers to manage the increased traffic

questions.correctText: Deploy a fiber distribution panel to organize and manage the fiber cables
questions.why: A fiber distribution panel centralizes fiber connections for tidy management and growth.
questions.whyWrong: More switches, routers or APs do not organize the physical fiber plant.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of SASE for an organization with a distributed workforce?

choices.text: Reduced latency for accessing centralized data centers
Enhanced encryption for data stored in cloud applications
Simplified management of security policies and configurations

questions.correctText: Simplified management of security policies and configurations
questions.why: SASE lets security policy be managed centrally and enforced for users anywhere.
questions.whyWrong: The site notes the other items may help but are not SASE's primary advantage.

questions.question: Snort runs as a network IDS and a rule matches during a scan. What happens?

choices.text: The entire packet is evaluated against all alert rules, then allowed to continue
The matching packet is dropped and scanning continues with new packets
The IDS alerts, stops checking remaining rules, and lets the packet continue
The source IP is blocked and its connection terminated

questions.correctText: The entire packet is evaluated against all alert rules, then allowed to continue
questions.why: An IDS inspects and logs but passes traffic through; it does not block.
questions.whyWrong: Dropping packets or blocking sources is IPS behavior, not IDS.

questions.question: Which command displays statistics for a given switchport on a Cisco switch?
questions.why: show interface reports the statistics for that interface.
questions.whyWrong: show route shows the routing table, show config the configuration, and show diagnostic hardware/software details.

questions.question: Packets are being discarded for being below the protocol's minimum size. What are they?
questions.why: Undersized frames are runts and get dropped.
questions.whyWrong: Giants and jumbo frames are oversized, and 'mini frames' is not a networking term.

questions.question: You need to add new features like advanced security and routing to an existing router without replacing hardware. What action is most likely?
questions.why: New firmware upgrades the device's built-in software and can add features.
questions.whyWrong: Patching only fixes flaws, IPv6 migration changes addressing, and cloning copies an existing setup.

questions.question: A new wireless router works for wired clients over a 1 Gbps fiber WAN, but wireless clients see high latency and slow downloads. What is most likely?

choices.text: The access point is experiencing RF interference
A fiber connection does not support wireless
A high signal-to-noise ratio on the wireless network
The network should use 802.11g WAPs to increase throughput

questions.correctText: The access point is experiencing RF interference
questions.why: RF interference forces retransmissions, which raise latency and cut wireless speed.
questions.whyWrong: Fiber is only the WAN link, a high signal-to-noise ratio is desirable, and dropping to 802.11g would be slower.

questions.question: After several breaches, which wireless security protocol gives stronger encryption and better brute-force protection?
questions.why: WPA3 is the newest standard, with stronger encryption and sign-in protections.
questions.whyWrong: WEP is obsolete and weak, WPA improved on it, and WPA2 has known flaws that WPA3 addressed.

questions.question: Which time protocol suits microsecond-level synchronization in a distributed system?
questions.why: PTP is built for microsecond-grade timing in fields like telecom and trading.
questions.whyWrong: NTP is coarser, and the site does not credit SNMP or TTP with this precision.

questions.question: Which topology is most appropriate for a direct, dedicated connection between two endpoints?
questions.why: Point-to-point is exactly a dedicated link between two endpoints.
questions.whyWrong: Bus shares one cable, hub-and-spoke centers on a hub, and hybrid mixes topologies without being a direct link.

questions.question: What is the network ID for host 189.76.60.164/26?
questions.why: A /26 block holds 64 addresses, and .164 falls in the block starting at .128.
questions.whyWrong: The other choices start the neighboring blocks that do not contain .164.

questions.question: What does the Nmap -O flag output?

choices.text: The operating system details of the target server
A list of IP addresses and the protocols they use
A list of open ports on the server
The versions of services running on the open ports

questions.correctText: The operating system details of the target server
questions.why: -O performs operating system detection on the target.
questions.whyWrong: Open ports are the default scan, service versions need -sV, and protocol listing is a different scan.

questions.question: Which DNS zone maps domain names to their IP addresses?
questions.why: A forward zone holds the name-to-address mappings.
questions.whyWrong: A reverse zone does the opposite, a secondary is a replica, and authoritative describes record authority rather than the mapping direction.

questions.question: Branch workers must open a page and click 'I agree' before proceeding. Which document are they agreeing to?
questions.why: Clicking agree to usage rules means accepting the acceptable use policy.
questions.whyWrong: An MOU is an inter-party understanding, an SLA sets service levels, and a EULA licenses software.

questions.question: A wireless network should identify itself to visitors by its network name across multiple APs. Which broadcast type?
questions.why: An ESSID lets several access points advertise one shared network name.
questions.whyWrong: A BSSID covers a single AP, while ARP and DHCP broadcasts happen after connection for addressing, not naming.

questions.question: Which cloud feature lets a customer carve out a logically isolated section of the cloud?
questions.why: A VPC is the customer's own isolated virtual network inside the cloud.
questions.whyWrong: SaaS delivers apps, IaC automates provisioning, and a CDN distributes content.

questions.question: You want any deviation from normal operation identified and addressed quickly. What should be implemented?

choices.text: An Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) detection system

questions.why: Anomaly alerting watches behavior continuously and flags departures from normal.
questions.whyWrong: An IPS matches known threats, APT detection is narrower, and NAC controls admission rather than alerting on behavior.

questions.question: Setting up a floor with VoIP phones and workstations on switch ports, what is the best configuration?

choices.text: Configure the voice VLAN on the switch ports where VoIP phones connect
Configure QoS to prioritize VLAN 100 over VLAN 200
Set the native VLAN to 200 for voice and VLAN 100 for data
Enable link aggregation on the ports connected to VoIP phones

questions.correctText: Configure the voice VLAN on the switch ports where VoIP phones connect
questions.why: Assigning the voice VLAN on those ports is the direct way to separate and prioritize voice.
questions.whyWrong: QoS is less direct here, native-VLAN assignment for voice is not best practice, and aggregation adds bandwidth, not voice priority.

questions.question: What is the term for attacking a smartphone through a weakness in the user's Bluetooth headset?
questions.why: Per the site, this Bluetooth attack is bluejacking - sending unsolicited messages to Bluetooth devices.
questions.whyWrong: A zero-day exploits an unpatched flaw, a Smurf attack floods with spoofed ICMP, and multiplexing is a signal-combining technique, not an attack.

questions.question: Which port number does HTTPS use?
questions.why: HTTPS runs on port 443 with encrypted transfer.
questions.whyWrong: 80 is HTTP, 123 is NTP, and 143 is IMAP.

questions.question: Which architecture should connect servers within a datacenter?
questions.why: Spine-and-leaf is the modern data center fabric that meshes leaf switches through spines for performance and redundancy.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the other options for this item.

questions.question: Which DNS record type designates the authoritative name servers for a domain?
questions.why: NS records name the domain's authoritative servers.
questions.whyWrong: AAAA maps to IPv6, MX routes mail, and CNAME creates an alias.

questions.question: Which DNS record type holds written information describing a domain's purpose, content or ownership?
questions.why: TXT records store human-readable text about the domain, including things like SPF data.
questions.whyWrong: CNAME aliases a name, PTR is reverse lookup, and AAAA maps to IPv6.

questions.question: A point-to-point router link over fiber does not come up after configuration. What is the problem?

choices.text: The cable is subject to crosstalk
The connection is suffering from EMI
The bend radius has been exceeded

questions.why: If the transceivers at each end use different wavelengths, they cannot communicate.
questions.whyWrong: Fiber is immune to crosstalk and EMI, and bend radius describes safe bending, not this failure.

questions.question: On a floor plan, which antenna setup for AP1/AP2/AP3 keeps the signal inside the building?

choices.text: 5 dB directional right for AP1, 5 dB directional left for AP2, 5 dB omnidirectional for AP3
5 dB omnidirectional for AP1, 5 dB directional left for AP2, 5 dB directional right for AP3
5 dB directional left for AP1, 5 dB omnidirectional for AP2, 5 dB directional right for AP3
5 dB directional right for AP1, 5 dB omnidirectional for AP2, 5 dB directional left for AP3

questions.correctText: 5 dB directional right for AP1, 5 dB omnidirectional for AP2, 5 dB directional left for AP3
questions.why: Directional antennas on the wall APs point inward and only the center AP is omnidirectional, containing the signal.
questions.whyWrong: The other layouts put an omnidirectional or wrongly aimed antenna on a wall, leaking signal outside.

questions.question: A network is split into multiple broadcast domains. Which device lets the segments communicate?
questions.why: A router (Layer 3) forwards traffic between broadcast domains.
questions.whyWrong: Bridges, switches (Layer 2) and hubs (Layer 1) cannot route between domains.

questions.question: Which Nmap flag gives the most accurate information about devices' operating systems?
questions.why: -O probes the host and infers its operating system from the responses.
questions.whyWrong: -sT is a TCP connect scan, -sU scans UDP, and -sV detects service versions.

questions.question: At which OSI layer is data encapsulated into segments?
questions.why: Layer 4 (transport) creates segments.
questions.whyWrong: Layer 3 makes packets, Layer 2 makes frames, and Layer 5 handles session data.

questions.question: Which network device operates at Layer 3?
questions.why: Routers forward packets between networks using IP addresses at Layer 3.
questions.whyWrong: Hubs and repeaters are Layer 1, and a bridge is Layer 2.

questions.question: Before a VoIP install, all switches were replaced with Layer 3 multilayer switches so VoIP can sit on separate VLANs with accurate routing. Which term best describes this?
