questions.why: Shrinking broadcast domains and routing between VLANs improves voice and video quality - performance optimization.
questions.whyWrong: Compliance enforcement is regulation-driven segmentation, a honeynet is a decoy, and public/private separation is a cloud-style split.

questions.question: Which plan dictates how an organization purchases, uses and disposes of network equipment?
questions.why: A system life cycle plan covers an asset from planning through retirement and disposal.
questions.whyWrong: The other plans cover operating through disruption, resuming after incidents, and responding to security events.

questions.question: A stateless firewall must allow HTTP from the 192.168.0.0/24 network. Which ACL is correct?

choices.text: PERMIT SRCIP:ANY SPORT:80 DSTIP:192.168.0.0/24 DPORT ANY

questions.why: Outbound web traffic goes from the internal network, any source port, to any destination on port 80.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the other ACLs; each either reverses the direction or pins the wrong ports.

questions.question: A new office build needs switch-to-workstation connections organized and manageable for future work. What should be implemented?

choices.text: Use a PDU to better manage electrical connections
Replace all Cat5e cables with Cat6 to increase speed
Install additional wireless access points to reduce cable clutter
Implement a patch panel to organize and connect switches to workstations

questions.correctText: Implement a patch panel to organize and connect switches to workstations
questions.why: A patch panel centralizes and labels the wired connections for easy changes and troubleshooting.
questions.whyWrong: A PDU manages power, faster cable does not organize anything, and more APs do not tidy wired runs.

questions.question: During a physical pen test, a man asks an employee to badge him in, claiming he forgot his card. What type of social engineering is that?
questions.why: Piggybacking is when the authorized person knowingly lets the intruder in.
questions.whyWrong: Tailgating is following in without the person's knowledge, shoulder surfing steals data by watching, and phishing uses deceptive messages.

questions.question: Web traffic to an e-commerce server rises but financial transactions do not. What kind of attack is it?
questions.why: A denial-of-service flood inflates traffic with non-customer requests that buy nothing.
questions.whyWrong: ARP spoofing redirects LAN traffic, phishing tricks users by message, and bluejacking sends Bluetooth messages.

questions.question: A 50-device branch needs simple, low-overhead routing plus high-throughput wired connectivity, cost-effectively. Which combination fits?

choices.text: OSPF; devices connected with a 100 Mbps Layer 2 switch
RIP; devices connected with a Gigabit Layer 2 switch
BGP; devices connected with a Gigabit Layer 3 switch
EIGRP; devices connected with an 802.11n wireless access point

questions.correctText: RIP; devices connected with a Gigabit Layer 2 switch
questions.why: RIP is simple and light for small networks, and a gigabit Layer 2 switch gives cheap wired speed.
questions.whyWrong: OSPF and BGP are heavier than a small branch needs, the 100 Mbps switch fails the throughput need, and wireless EIGRP gear sacrifices wired reliability.

questions.question: Users see slow, intermittent access to an internal website; the server was assigned an incorrect default gateway. What resolves it?

choices.text: Reset the switch the server is connected to
Assign a new IP address to the server
Configure a static route on the router for the server's IP
Reconfigure the server's default gateway to the correct IP address

questions.correctText: Reconfigure the server's default gateway to the correct IP address
questions.why: Fixing the server's gateway restores its path to other subnets.
questions.whyWrong: Resetting the switch or changing the IP does not correct the bad setting, and a router static route cannot fix the server's own gateway.

questions.question: Unauthorized devices plugging into Ethernet ports are a risk. Which feature restricts access by allowed MAC addresses?
questions.why: Port security defines which MAC addresses may use each switch port.
questions.whyWrong: VLANs segment logically, DHCP snooping blocks rogue DHCP servers, and STP prevents loops.

questions.question: Which IEEE specification describes network authentication?
questions.why: 802.1X authenticates users/devices before opening a port for access.
questions.whyWrong: 802.1d is spanning tree, 802.3ad is link aggregation, and 802.3af is PoE.

questions.question: In a data center, which component can be fitted with a lock to protect network connections and cabling?
questions.why: Lockable patch panels secure the physical connections against tampering.
questions.whyWrong: Transceivers and cables have no locking mechanism, and an SVI is virtual software.

questions.question: Which environmental factor is critical for preventing equipment corrosion and static buildup?
questions.why: Controlled humidity prevents both corrosion and static accumulation.
questions.whyWrong: Air conditioning manages temperature and can worsen static if humidity drops, filtration handles dust, and suppression handles fires.

questions.question: Two WAN router interfaces need exactly two addresses with maximum conservation. Which mask fits?
questions.why: A /30 leaves two usable host addresses - one for each router.
questions.whyWrong: /32 has no usable hosts, and /28 and /29 waste extra addresses.

questions.question: Which tool attaches an RJ-45 connector to UTP cable wired to the 568B standard?
questions.why: A crimper presses the cable's wires into the connector's pins.
questions.whyWrong: A punchdown tool seats wires in blocks, a fusion splicer joins fiber, and snips only cut cable.

questions.why: DNS over TLS encrypts queries and runs on its dedicated standard port (853).
questions.whyWrong: DNSSEC authenticates but does not encrypt, WPAD locates proxy configs, and DoH encrypts over HTTPS rather than the DNS-port model described.

questions.question: A Cat 6 cable runs a 10 Gbps link over 60 meters; it is intact but errors and disconnects are frequent. What is most likely?
questions.why: Cat 6 only carries 10 Gbps to about 55 m; at 60 m it is out of spec and Cat 6a is needed.
questions.whyWrong: Attenuation is generic, no interference source is mentioned, and transposed pairs would stop the link entirely rather than make it flaky.

questions.question: Which ports do SMTP and SNMP use?
questions.why: SMTP sends mail on 25 and SNMP manages devices on 161.
questions.whyWrong: The other pairs belong to HTTPS, SMB, RDP and Telnet combinations.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used for centralized AAA for remote access users?
questions.why: RADIUS centralizes authentication, authorization and accounting for remote access.
questions.whyWrong: POP3 retrieves mail, SNMP manages devices, and LDAP is a directory service without RADIUS's session handling.

questions.question: During a power outage, which security control would most likely still be usable?
questions.why: A traditional mechanical lock needs no power to keep working.
questions.whyWrong: Scanners, detectors and cameras all need electricity.

questions.question: Routing prefixes are assigned in blocks by IANA via regional registries. What are the unique identifiers managing these assignments called?
questions.why: An autonomous system number identifies the operator's routing domain for BGP.
questions.whyWrong: The site does not detail the other terms for this item.

questions.question: What is the broadcast address for host 201.58.12.245/28 - as revealed by the site?
questions.why: The site revealed 201.58.12.255 as the last address of the range containing .245.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not break down the other addresses individually.

questions.question: Which cloud model ensures the strongest security for a company's resources?
questions.why: A private cloud is dedicated to one company, giving exclusive control and isolation.
questions.whyWrong: Hybrid still includes public elements, public is shared with everyone, and community is shared with peer organizations.

questions.question: What type of IPv6 address is ::1?
questions.why: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address, like 127.0.0.1 in IPv4.
questions.whyWrong: It targets the host itself, not a subnet, group or the public internet.

questions.question: A user's laptop cannot connect to corporate wireless. What should the technician do FIRST per the methodology?
questions.why: Identifying the problem - gathering information and symptoms - is step one.
questions.whyWrong: Planning is step 4, implementing step 5 and verifying step 6.

questions.question: Which device uses ACLs to prevent unauthorized access into company systems?
questions.why: A firewall enforces ACL rules that allow or deny traffic into the network.
questions.whyWrong: An IDS only monitors, a load balancer spreads work, and a content filter screens content.

questions.question: A technician downloaded the newest switch OS. What should he do FIRST when updating?

choices.text: Test the OS on one of the production switches
Power cycle the company's border router
Backup the current configuration for each switch
Install during non-business hours to test the system

questions.correctText: Backup the current configuration for each switch
questions.why: Backing up current configs first allows a rollback if the new OS misbehaves.
questions.whyWrong: Off-hours installation is wise but comes second; the site does not endorse testing on production gear or cycling the border router first.

questions.question: Which fire suppression system uses halocarbon or inert gas to suffocate a fire?
questions.why: Clean agent systems flood the room with gas that displaces oxygen.
questions.whyWrong: Wet pipe and pre-action systems use water sprinklers, and HVAC is climate control, not suppression.

questions.question: Free restaurant Wi-Fi (no portal, no password) disconnects users after 30 minutes. Which technique lets you reconnect?
questions.why: The AP evidently blocks by MAC after 30 minutes, so presenting a new MAC address reconnects you.
questions.whyWrong: IP spoofing fails because access is blocked before an IP is issued, and there is no password for guessing attacks to target.

questions.question: Which cloud gateway type primarily translates network addresses between on-premises and cloud resources?
questions.why: A NAT gateway performs the address translation and shields private instances from inbound initiation.
questions.whyWrong: A CASB enforces security policy, a CDN distributes content, and cloud storage gateways connect to storage.

questions.question: What distinguishes Security Service Edge (SSE) from traditional network security?

choices.text: SSE leverages cloud-based security services to protect distributed users and devices
SSE prioritizes network performance over security functionalities
SSE relies on physical appliances at the network perimeter
SSE focuses solely on securing endpoints within the corporate network

questions.correctText: SSE leverages cloud-based security services to protect distributed users and devices
questions.why: SSE moves security enforcement into the cloud for users and devices wherever they are.
questions.whyWrong: It moves away from perimeter appliances, covers more than corporate endpoints, and does not put performance above security.

questions.question: After patching, older PCs with non-gigabit cards all disconnected. What prevents this at the next update?

choices.text: Require the patching server to update the oldest PCs off-hours
Disable automatic driver updates to PCs from the patching server
Enable automatic rebooting of the PCs after patching
Throttle the patching server's connection speed to match older PCs

questions.correctText: Disable automatic driver updates to PCs from the patching server
questions.why: An automatically pushed driver likely broke the old cards; disabling automatic driver updates and testing drivers first prevents a repeat.
questions.whyWrong: Timing, throttling and rebooting do not address driver compatibility.

questions.question: Which component ensures continuous power to critical equipment during outages?
questions.why: A UPS supplies immediate backup power when the mains fail.
questions.whyWrong: A PDU only distributes power and a surge protector only absorbs spikes; a generator is backup too, but the UPS is the purpose-built answer per the site.

questions.question: A speed test reports 99.79 / 116.61. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: The website downloads data to its server at 99.79 Mbps and uploads from its server at 116.61 Mbps
The PC downloaded 99.79 MB from the website and uploaded 116.61 MB to it
The PC downloads faster than it uploads because the connection is asynchronous
The PC is receiving data at 99.79 Mbps and sending data to the server at 116.61 Mbps

questions.correctText: The PC is receiving data at 99.79 Mbps and sending data to the server at 116.61 Mbps
questions.why: The first figure is the measured download rate and the second the upload rate, both in Mbps at the PC.

questions.question: Which error is received if raw data is accidentally changed in transit?

questions.whyWrong: Runts and giants are size faults, and encapsulation is a framing process, not an error.

questions.question: Designing a redundant distance-vector network, what advertises failed routes with an infinite metric to prevent loops?
questions.why: Route poisoning marks a failed route unreachable with an over-maximum metric.

questions.question: Which authentication protocol is strongest for remote access VPN connections?
questions.why: EAP-TLS uses certificates for mutual authentication with strong encryption.
questions.whyWrong: PAP sends credentials in plaintext, and CHAP/MS-CHAP depend on shared secrets.

questions.question: A facility must verify each person's identity at the server room and stop tailgating. Which solution best fits?

choices.text: Implement a biometric reader at the datacenter entrance and require passage through a mantrap
Implement a CCTV camera and a proximity reader at the data center entrance
Implement a security guard at the facility entrance and a keypad at the data center entrance
Implement a biometric reader at the facility entrance and a proximity card at the data center entrance

questions.correctText: Implement a biometric reader at the datacenter entrance and require passage through a mantrap
questions.why: Biometrics verify the individual, and a mantrap physically enforces one person at a time.
questions.whyWrong: Cards can be stolen and do not stop tailgating, guards and keypads are weaker, and CCTV only records.

questions.question: A new web app needs minimal latency and DNS that always serves the most updated records it manages itself. Which option fits?

choices.text: Configure a forwarding DNS server to redirect queries upward
Set up a non-authoritative DNS server

questions.why: An authoritative server answers directly from the records it manages, so answers are current.

questions.question: Several users cannot reach resources in other VLANs; affected ports' VLAN assignments are wrong. What should be checked first?
questions.why: The VLAN database holds each port's assignments, which is where the stated fault lives.
questions.whyWrong: Routing tables, DHCP options and DNS settings do not define switch-port VLAN membership.

questions.question: On an 802.11n network most users reach 300 Mbps, but a few n cards cap at 108 Mbps. What should the technician do?

choices.text: Roll back the WLAN card firmware

questions.why: Outdated or corrupt drivers stop cards from using n's faster rates; updating the driver restores full speed.
questions.whyWrong: The site did not single out the other options for this item.

questions.question: A new DMZ web server must be verified as hardened, with only inbound HTTPS allowed and HTTP blocked. Which tool checks that?
questions.why: A port scanner shows exactly which ports are open, confirming only 443 is reachable.
